t: Three Maine towns put data center bans or pauses to voters
b: North Berwick skipped a moratorium to let voters decide on a permanent ban.
iw: Possible permanent bans

t: Archbald unanimously denies the 14-building Wildcat Ridge campus
b: The 578-acre plan included 588 diesel backup generators. After nine hearings, council rejected it; an appeal is expected. Four more campuses are proposed in the borough.
iw: Hyperscale campus denied

t: Somerset County requires data centers to make 150% of their own power
b: Unanimous ordinance also sets 1,000-foot setbacks from homes. No project had been filed.
iw: Very demanding power rule

t: Advocates count 110 New Jersey towns with data center bans
b: The group is pressing Gov. Sherrill for a three-year statewide moratorium.
iw: Breadth of local bans

t: South Berwick adopts a 180-day pause for facilities over 10,000 sq ft
b: Retroactive to July 14. It expires just before the state's recommendations are due Jan. 29, 2027.
iw: Low size threshold

t: State fines Vineland data center $1.07M for 62 unpermitted generators
b: DataOne must get permits within 45 days or stop running the gas generators. Regulators called it the largest enforcement action against a data center in the state.
iw: Enforcement against on-site power

t: Massena declines to adopt a data center moratorium
b: St. Lawrence County had urged its towns to consider pauses.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Harvie calls for a data center moratorium in his race against Fitzpatrick
b: His first general-election TV ad, a shift from his earlier call for strict rules. As a county commissioner he voted in 2020 for a tax break on the Falls Township site that became Amazon's data center; Fitzpatrick backs transparency and ratepayer bills but not a pause.
iw: Pause pledge in a swing district

t: Butternuts adopts a data center moratorium
b: Unanimous vote in Otsego County, alongside a battery storage moratorium, after a Sept. 9 hearing on one-year pauses. Note: no news story found; the vote is reported only in Citizen Portal's AI-written meeting summary, and the town's own site lists the hearing.
iw: Rural town pause

t: Brick introduces a ban; Bridgewater opts for rules
b: Bridgewater already doesn't permit data centers anywhere but avoided an outright ban over lawsuit concerns.
iw: More towns acting

t: Greenfield moves toward a one-year pause as more cities weigh limits
b: New Bedford is considering a ban; Northampton and Easthampton are eyeing moratoriums.
iw: More pauses likely

t: Minogue says Massachusetts can't handle more data center demand
b: Healey's Republican opponent shows little interest in new data centers either.
iw: Both candidates skeptical

t: House Democrats plan a 24-month moratorium bill for 2027
b: Announced the same day Ayotte said she opposes any data center in the state.
iw: Bipartisan appetite for a pause

t: Springhill Township adopts data center and power plant rules
b: Supervisors unanimously limited data centers and their power plants to conditional uses in industrial zones, after a Sept. 3 resolution barred applications in the meantime. The push began when power producer Nadara disclosed a purchase option on 800 acres near Gans; no application has been filed.
iw: Temporary township ban

t: Lamont: Connecticut is the wrong place for massive AI data centers
b: He'd consider projects that bring their own power, pass utility regulators and win local approval. Earlier he urged the state to slow down new data centers.
iw: Governor discourages hyperscale projects

t: Fazio wants to end Connecticut's data center tax breaks
b: The Republican nominee opposes incentives but not an outright ban.
iw: Both candidates cool on incentives

t: Gorham moves toward a permanent data center ban
b: Councilors unanimously asked the planning board to hold a hearing on a permanent ban. A 180-day moratorium adopted 7–0 in June is in place, and no data center has been proposed in town.
iw: Possible permanent ban

t: Hopkinton bans data centers in every zoning district
b: The council voted 5–0 for the permanent ban after a 60-day emergency moratorium in September; there are no current plans for a data center in town.
iw: Short emergency pause

t: Data centers must report water and energy use every six months
b: S3379 also came with state guidance for towns negotiating community benefits agreements. Advocates called it too weak and renewed calls for a moratorium.
iw: New disclosure duties

t: Orangetown pauses data centers and battery storage for six months
b: The 180-day moratorium exempts applications filed before July 1, so DataBank's proposed second building near Lake Tappan, already under a full environmental impact study, goes on. Residents objected to the carve-out.
iw: Pause, but the pending project is exempt

t: Judge blocks four new diesel generators at Lowell's data center
b: Residents challenged the state's air permit for eight more generators; four already installed can keep running.
iw: Court limits backup power expansion

t: Vineland weighs a revised 300 MW self-powered AI campus
b: The DataOne/Nebius plan would generate its own power; residents raised LNG storage, emissions, water and noise concerns.
iw: Large project still under review

t: More than 30 New Jersey towns ban data centers by mid-August
b: Includes Jersey City, Bayonne, Howell, Warren, Madison, East Brunswick and Stafford, per an advocacy group's count.
iw: Bans spreading statewide

t: Utility study eyes a large load at Bow's former coal plant
b: Eversource is studying service for a possible hyperscale project at the Merrimack Station site, per FERC filings. Gov. Ayotte opposes it.
iw: Early-stage project facing opposition

t: Westerly adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: Voted 7–0 to study grid, water and emergency service impacts.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Brookhaven adopts an 18-month data center moratorium
b: Unanimous vote on Long Island two days after the state's executive order, aimed in part at a proposed Yaphank project.
iw: Long pause in a large suburban town

t: East Greenbush passes the first local pause after the state order
b: A six-month moratorium on data center development and operation in Rensselaer County.
iw: Six-month town pause

t: PJM's capacity auction hits the price cap again
b: The 2028/29 auction cleared at the $325/MW-day cap with a reserve shortfall. The market monitor attributes about 46% of capacity charges over four auctions to data centers.
iw: Mounting pressure to make data centers pay

t: New Jersey puts data centers in their own rate class
b: P.L.2026 c.32 covers new and existing data centers of 50 MW or more, requiring them to pay for their energy and grid upgrades and commit to 85% take-or-pay for ten years.
iw: Binding cost rules, including for existing sites

t: Seneca Nation and Sierra Club sue over the STAMP zoning agreement
b: The suit says a deal barring the Town of Alabama from changing its zoning without the county agency's approval is void. A $19.4 billion, 500 MW Stream campus is under review there.
iw: Could unwind the zoning a major campus relies on

t: New Haven considers a 12-month data center moratorium
b: A working group would recommend zoning standards within six months.
iw: Possible city pause

t: House votes 197–5 to repeal the data center sales tax break
b: The exemption is projected to cost $517 million a year by 2030. The Senate added similar language to a tax bill, and the House also passed a pause bill.
iw: Could end a major incentive

t: Healey stops accepting data center sales tax exemption applications
b: Paused the 2024 incentive and issued a framework of expectations on cost, water and community engagement, later made binding by Executive Order 658.
iw: Incentive paused indefinitely

t: Bethlehem adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: The Albany County town acted before the statewide executive order.
iw: One-year town pause

t: All six Rhode Island data center bills die
b: Proposals on 30-year tax breaks, cost allocation, siting and water reporting were held for study. No statewide moratorium bill was filed.
iw: No incentives, no rules

t: American Tower withdraws East Greenwich application after a ban
b: The township banned data centers while the Mount Royal application was pending.
iw: Project withdrawn

t: West Haven adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: Unanimous; server rooms incidental to a building's main use are exempt. Mayor Dorinda Borer proposed it.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Developer sues Monroe Township for over $300 million over its ban
b: Moved to federal court in July. The outcome will signal how far New Jersey towns can go.
iw: Tests whether local bans hold

t: Allegany permanently bans data centers and crypto facilities
b: Local Law 3 applies in every zoning district. No project had been proposed; the board cited energy use and farmland loss.
iw: Permanent townwide ban

t: Frelinghuysen bans large data centers; Blairstown caps size at 5,000 sq ft
b: The county planning director says 18 of Warren County's 22 towns now have data center protections, many based on a county model ordinance.
iw: Most of a county now restrictive

t: Holyoke becomes the first Massachusetts city to ban AI data centers
b: A citywide ban, as other western Massachusetts cities weigh pauses.
iw: Citywide ban

t: Veto of Vermont's data center deployment bill is sustained
b: The House upheld the governor's veto of H.727 by 83–52, short of the votes needed to override.
iw: No new state framework

t: Sanford pauses data centers, stalling a 1,000-acre campus
b: A 91-day pause on the Sanford Woods campus along the Mousam River, later extended 180 days.
iw: Pause blocks a major proposal

t: Coalition asks Sherrill to use emergency powers for a moratorium
b: Cited rising bills, water use in the Pinelands aquifer and PFAS risks. She chose rules instead of a pause.
iw: Pressure for a state pause

t: S9144A would pause big data centers for three years
b: Covers facilities of 20 MW and up and asks regulators to keep costs off other ratepayers. Recommitted to committee in May; the narrower one-year bill passed instead.
iw: Longer statewide pause, stalled

t: Lysander adopts a six-month pause amid a 300 MW campus fight
b: Unanimous vote in Onondaga County after more than 1,800 residents petitioned against Ranalli Super DC's 300 MW grid request for a 124-acre site; no application has been filed. Clay and Manlius later adopted one-year pauses. The pause expires Nov. 7.
iw: Pause aimed at a specific large project

t: Smithfield bans data centers in every zoning district
b: Passed 4–1, a day after Hanton City Investments filed for a complex near Fidelity's campus. The developer is appealing the town's incompleteness ruling.
iw: Townwide ban, contested

t: Oneonta pauses data centers and crypto mining for a year
b: Unanimous 12-month moratorium in Otsego County after more than 700 residents petitioned against Eco-Yotta's proposal on County Road 9, which will no longer be processed. The supervisor hopes to follow with a ban.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Townships use 180-day planning pauses to write data center rules
b: Pennsylvania towns can't ban a land use outright, so many use a curative amendment to pause applications while drafting ordinances.
iw: Short pauses spreading

t: Harrison Township adopts its own data center ban
b: One of several Gloucester County bans this spring.
iw: Township ban

t: Bills to end data center incentives and set large-load rules die
b: SB 245 would have ended data center tax incentives; HB 5469 would have regulated data centers drawing power from plants like Millstone. Lawmakers said interest faded as high power costs deterred developers.
iw: Status quo holds

t: Morris pauses data centers and battery storage
b: The posted text sets 12 months; some coverage describes two years.
iw: Town pause

t: Mansfield adopts the state's first comprehensive data center bylaw
b: Voted at annual town meeting in May.
iw: Detailed local rules

t: Monroe Township bans data centers in every zone
b: Effective May 13. The ordinance says no prior approval vests a right to build one, closing a warehouse-to-data-center conversion.
iw: Township-wide ban

t: Logan Township bans data centers townwide
b: Also blocks existing warehouses from converting, amid confusion over a Route 130 project.
iw: Township ban

t: Phillipsburg and Waterford ban data centers in all zones
b: Waterford cited its status as a Pinelands community.
iw: Town bans

t: Kenilworth's mayor defends CoreWeave's AI campus at the old Merck site
b: She says the redevelopment replaces lost tax revenue; packed council meetings followed.
iw: Local backing for a major project

t: FERC extends PJM's capacity price cap for two more auctions
b: Grew out of Shapiro's 2025 settlement with PJM. The next uncapped auction is May 2027.
iw: Caps consumer costs; data center rules unchanged

t: Archbald rejects an 18-building campus near Staback Park
b: Unanimous denial of Archbald 1 LLC's 400-acre application.
iw: Project denied

t: Over 200 pack a hearing against the $19.4B STAMP data center
b: Seneca citizens and neighbors urged the county agency to reject the campus and its roughly $1.46 billion tax break request.
iw: Organized opposition to a flagship project

t: PennFuture calls for a statewide data center moratorium
b: The environmental group says development should wait for rules on siting, water and clean energy.
iw: Organized push for a state pause

t: House kills a one-year statewide data center ban
b: HB 1265 was found inexpedient to legislate on a voice vote.
iw: Statewide ban rejected

t: Dryden makes data centers a prohibited use
b: Follows an 18-month moratorium the Tompkins County town adopted in July 2024 after a developer proposal.
iw: Permanent zoning prohibition

t: Pemberton becomes the first New Jersey town to ban data centers
b: The Burlington County ordinance prohibits building or operating them.
iw: Township ban

t: Prevailing wage now applies to data center construction
b: P.L.2025 c.335 covers projects of 5 MW or more starting on or after March 1, 2026.
iw: Higher construction costs

t: PJM governors and the White House issue joint principles
b: Called for affordability, reliability, market reform and a longer price cap.
iw: Regional pressure on large-load costs

t: East Fishkill pauses data centers for three years
b: Unanimous vote; the moratorium runs to July 1, 2029, one of the longest in the state.
iw: Three-year halt

t: DeWitt bars data center permits through 2027
b: The Onondaga County town's moratorium cites the state Senate's proposed three-year pause.
iw: Town pause through 2027

t: Olyphant halts new data centers for six months
b: Council voted 4–3 against a zoning amendment that would have limited data centers to about 1,000 industrial acres near the Triboro Industrial Park, then opened a 180-day curative amendment to rewrite it. No application is pending.
iw: Six-month pause

t: Montgomery's data center ban challenged in court
b: E. Kahn Development Corp. sued over the ban on a former commercial site.
iw: Ban under legal challenge

t: Lowell pauses new or expanded data centers for a year
b: Home to the state's largest data center, Markley's former Prince Spaghetti site.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Westfield adopts a one-year moratorium on additional data centers
b: It doesn't immediately affect Servistar's proposed 274 MW, 10-building campus, which would be New England's largest.
iw: Pause, but the big project is outside it

t: Vermont's AI data center moratorium bill never leaves committee
b: S.205 would have paused AI data centers until July 2030.
iw: Statewide pause died

t: A wave of Maine towns pause data centers after the veto
b: Bangor, Brunswick, Westbrook, Gorham, Gray, Scarborough and Saco approved pauses of 91 to 180 days starting in May.
iw: Local pauses filling the state gap

t: Archbald creates four data center zoning districts over objections
b: Passed 4–2 with one abstention; no residents spoke in favor. The districts made the borough a magnet for proposals.
iw: Zoning opened land to data centers

t: Lewiston votes down a $300 million data center
b: Rejected after swift opposition. A $5 billion Wiscasset proposal was paused a month earlier.
iw: Project rejected

t: STAMP data center approval rescinded after a Seneca lawsuit
b: The Tonawanda Seneca Nation and Sierra Club sued over $472 million in tax breaks approved without full environmental review. The developer withdrew to propose a larger project.
iw: First approval undone, though a bigger plan followed

t: Pennsylvania's data center equipment sales tax exemption
b: Still in force, though Shapiro's August order ties new certifications to his GRID standards.
iw: Valuable incentive, now conditioned

t: Connecticut's 2021 data center tax incentive is still on the books
b: Offers 20- or 30-year sales and property tax waivers for large investments. Only one company has used it.
iw: Generous incentive, little used

t: Warmington calls Ayotte's budget-based moratorium too slow
b: Both candidates for governor favor freezing new data center permits. Ayotte says she opposes the Bow and Nottingham proposals; Warmington argues a pause in next year's budget could come after a big project lands.
iw: Pause likely whoever wins

t: Westfield denies a permit extension for the Servistar hyperscale campus
b: The unanimous vote lets the 2021 special permit lapse at the end of October, likely ending what would have been New England's largest data center. Servistar never bought the land; it has 20 days to appeal.
iw: Major proposal likely ends

t: Bucksport adopts a six-month data center moratorium
b: The 5–2 vote covers all data centers, not just large ones. At least two data center firms have eyed the mostly vacant former Verso paper mill, though none has applied.
iw: Six-month town pause

t: Over 100 rally in Bow against a data center at Merrimack Station
b: Residents protested outside a select board meeting over a possible hyperscale project at the shuttered coal plant, citing water, noise and property values. No application has been filed.
iw: Organized opposition

t: New Haven adopts a 12-month data center moratorium
b: Alders present voted unanimously, with an exception for quantum computing. Without the pause, data centers would be allowed as of right in industrial zones and the Union Station area.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Senate Republicans back Ayotte and pledge data center legislation
b: Carson said the caucus agrees with the governor on halting data center construction and will pursue a bill to keep the costs off taxpayers. She gave no timeline.
iw: Both parties now favor a pause

t: Nottingham voters approve a 12-month data center moratorium, 1,335 to 143
b: The special election followed a warehouse-conversion proposal withdrawn amid backlash. The planning board is drafting zoning that could ban data centers permanently.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Regulators order Rhode Island Energy to propose a tariff for 20 MW-plus loads
b: The rate case ruling requires a filing by Dec. 31 meant to keep data centers and other very large loads from shifting costs, straining reliability or causing rate shock. Legislative cost bills had stalled.
iw: Cost protections coming

t: FERC orders ISO New England to justify or rewrite its large-load rules
b: The show cause order preliminarily finds ISO-NE's tariff may be unjust because it lacks provisions for studying, connecting and charging data centers and other big loads, including co-located ones.
iw: New England grid rules in flux

t: SB 439 dies after amendments to make data centers allowed by right
b: Democrats proposed it to give towns tools to regulate data centers. Republican changes would have required towns to allow them in commercial and industrial zones, and the bill died at adjournment.
iw: Towns keep current siting powers

t: Maine bars new data centers from key business tax breaks
b: LD 713 makes data centers that start operating after July ineligible for the business equipment tax exemption and the Dirigo program. The state must study other incentives and report by Nov. 4.
iw: Loss of state tax incentives

t: Canterbury voters change zoning to ban data centers
b: The March town meeting acted with no project proposed, one of several New England towns moving preemptively.
iw: Townwide ban

t: House kills a bill creating New Hampshire's first data center incentives
b: HB 1739 would have offered property tax deals and business tax credits, conditioned on paying grid costs and joining demand response. It was found inexpedient to legislate on a voice vote.
iw: No new incentives

t: Energy affordability bill in conference could add data center rules
b: The House version would create a data center-specific tariff; the Senate's largely writes in Healey's expectations on clean power, water and community benefits. Negotiators were reconciling them in September.
iw: Possible binding cost rules

t: Wiscasset pauses talks on a $5 billion data center on town land
b: The select board halted discussions after resident pushback and is drafting a review process with no set end date. The plan also cost the town a $240,000 county housing award for the same land.
iw: Indefinite halt to a major proposal

t: LiquidCool plans Maine's first large AI data center at the former Loring base
b: The Limestone project would fill an existing warehouse, with a Versant deal for 24 MW on top of 2 MW already in the building. The company says its immersion cooling avoids water use.
iw: Reuses an existing building

t: Consent order lets Markley install disputed generators while the appeal is pending
b: Residents learned of the order only in January 2026. Their lawsuit says it exceeded MassDEP's authority, and in August 2026 a judge stayed the permit.
iw: Construction allowed before a final permit

t: Residents organize after a $5 billion data center plan surfaces in Wiscasset
b: The plan for town-owned land along the Back River became public in mid-September. Neighbors formed Protect Wiscasset, saying little was disclosed about the end user, power source or grid impacts.
iw: Organized local opposition

t: Tax break revives a Westfield hyperscale plan worth up to $4 billion
b: At a state hearing on the exemption's rules, Westmass called the incentive critical to Servistar's 10- to 14-building plan. The Conservation Law Foundation urged stronger energy, water and efficiency safeguards.
iw: Incentive revived a hyperscale plan

t: New Hampshire lets off-grid power plants sell directly to big users
b: HB 672 exempts generators that never connect to the grid from utility regulation and renewable standards, a path for data centers to bring their own power. Siting, zoning and environmental permits still apply.
iw: Easier on-site power

t: Lowell neighbors' appeal of the data center's air permit is turned away
b: A hearing officer found seven of the eight residents lacked standing and in December recommended upholding the permit, which the commissioner later did. The residents then took the case to Superior Court.
iw: Agency challenge rejected

t: MassDEP approves eight more diesel generators at Lowell's Markley data center
b: The air plan brings the site to 27 generators and 16 cooling towers, some within 100 feet of homes. Opponents say it was approved without a cumulative impact analysis or state environmental review.
iw: Backup power expansion allowed

t: Bloomfield commissioners balk at a data center near Bradley airport
b: Members raised noise, building height, airport proximity and lost open space when the proposal came up in June 2025. A year later it still had not been approved.
iw: Proposal stalled

t: Maine law caps data centers' share of on-site power at a Millinocket mill
b: Emergency law LD 912 strips a generator's utility exemption if more than 25% of its capacity serves data centers. It targets the former Great Northern mill site, keeping its on-site hydropower available to other employers.
iw: Limits data center access to cheap hydropower

t: Rhode Island's 30-year data center tax break bills are held for study
b: S0921 and H6097 offered sales and property tax relief for $200 million investments in enterprise or opportunity zones, $400 million elsewhere. The tax administrator flagged weak job requirements; similar 2026 bills also stalled.
iw: Incentive not enacted

t: Waterford lets NE Edge hand its Millstone data center deal to a subsidiary
b: The 2–1 vote kept alive a 2023 host agreement worth $231 million over 30 years, with building permits due by March 2026. The Siting Council had rejected a key petition in 2024; a project database now lists the deal as terminated.
iw: Kept a stalled project alive

t: Bill to repeal towns' temporary moratorium power is tabled
b: SB 163 would have repealed RSA 674:23, the law towns use to adopt temporary building moratoriums. It passed the Senate, but the House laid it on the table in June 2025, leaving that authority in place as data center fights reached New Hampshire towns.
iw: Local pause power intact

t: Massachusetts creates a 20-year sales tax exemption for large data centers
b: The Mass Leads Act covers equipment, software, electricity and construction for sites of at least 100,000 sq ft, $50 million and 100 jobs. Certification rules went to a hearing in August 2025; Healey paused applications in June 2026.
iw: Valuable incentive, now paused

t: Wallingford rezones to allow data centers in its Watershed Interchange District
b: The town, which has its own electric utility, opened the district to data centers as other Connecticut towns moved to restrict them.
iw: Opens land to data centers

t: Groton caps data centers at 12,500 square feet, shutting out hyperscale projects
b: Adopted after a 2022 moratorium, the rules also bar water cooling. A developer sued for more than $5 billion, and towns as far away as Georgia now cite the rules as a model.
iw: Effective ban on large facilities

t: Loudoun's final vote on its 12-month pause moves to Nov. 17
b: Deferred from Oct. 20 so staff can gather more information. The pause would be retroactive to Sept. 15; 33 data center and substation applications are active.
iw: Pause in the densest data center market

t: Loudoun campus on 342 forested acres is deferred indefinitely
b: The applicant pulled its board hearing after the planning commission unanimously recommended denial.
iw: Project stalled

t: Leesburg march calls for a statewide data center moratorium
b: Part of a series of rallies organized with the Chesapeake Climate Action Network.
iw: Organized pressure for a state pause

t: Spanberger rules out a statewide data center moratorium
b: She called local pauses a local choice and pointed to her cost rules instead.
iw: No state pause

t: Spotsylvania backs a call for a statewide moratorium
b: Supervisors voted 4–2 to support Sen. Glen Sturtevant's request to the governor. Eight data centers are in the works in the county.
iw: Local pressure for a state pause

t: Moratorium bills stack up for Virginia's 2027 session
b: SB 843 from Sens. Perry and Roem would block data center permits from July 2027 to July 2030. Del. Shin and Sen. Sturtevant have their own versions.
iw: Possible statewide pause in 2027

t: QTS terminates the 2,100-acre Digital Gateway near Manassas
b: QTS withdrew its Virginia Supreme Court petitions, the last effort to revive rezonings that courts voided over flawed hearing notices. Compass and Prince William County had already dropped out.
iw: Largest proposed corridor killed

t: Project Flash, Crusoe's proposed Franklin County data center, is dropped
b: Residents found the project through public records requests: a 50–100 MW campus at the county's Summit View Business Park near Rocky Mount. A supervisor told a community meeting it would not proceed, but warned nothing stops another proposal.
iw: Project cancelled

t: Christiansburg ends by-right data centers
b: Voted 6–0 to require conditional use permits for data centers in the general industrial zone, where they had been allowed by right. The mayor said it could slow or halt applications; planners will refine the town's definition.
iw: Slower approvals

t: Developers pull the 900 MW Remington Innovation Campus hours before review
b: The six-building, three-substation plan, partly on land owned by Supervisor Daron Culbertson, was withdrawn the morning planners were to take it up. It was the third major Remington-area application pulled in a month.
iw: Application withdrawn

t: Federal suit over Amazon's Louisa site moves forward
b: A federal judge let neighbor Austin Newsom's private nuisance claim proceed, rejecting Amazon's argument that brown tap water, noise, dust and light from the Northeast Creek construction were insubstantial; a separate injunction claim was dismissed.
iw: Litigation risk

t: Warner's first reelection ad focuses on data centers
b: He now says data centers need to cover their own costs, after earlier calling them a local issue.
iw: Senior Democrat turns critical

t: Data Center Fair Share Act would tie highway funds to data center tariffs
b: Rep. Suhas Subramanyam's H.R. 10322 would make utilities recover the full cost of grid upgrades from customers of 100 MW or more, and withhold federal highway funds from states that don't adopt the standard.
iw: Federal cost pressure

t: West Virginia law strips local control over certified data centers
b: HB 2014 lets the state certify microgrid districts and high-impact data centers, bars local zoning, noise and building rules for them, and sends most new property tax to the state.
s: WV Energy and Data Center Tracker
iw: Local governments can't block certified projects

t: Lawmakers approve certification rules for microgrids and data centers
b: HB 4983 makes developers flag projects that would place an inordinate burden on neighbors. A transparency amendment was voted down.
iw: Fast-track framework stays intact

t: Bill to restore local control over data centers stalls
b: SB 658, backed by Tucker County residents, never left committee before the session ended. House Speaker Roger Hanshaw said changes to the 2025 law were premature.
iw: Preemption survives

t: State promises a citizen advisory council at a Tucker County forum
b: More than 150 people attended the panel near a proposed Fundamental Data campus and gas plant.
iw: Process, not new limits

t: Court dismisses Mingo County residents' suit over data center power plants
b: Residents challenged two TransGas facilities planned to power data centers near Holden and Wharncliffe.
iw: Legal challenge fails

t: Beshear order bars passing data center costs to other ratepayers
b: Executive Order 2026-494 also lets agencies deny permits on water and air grounds and expects full tax payment. Local approval is still up to communities.
iw: New cost and permit conditions

t: Kentucky data center guardrails stripped on the session's last day
b: Rep. Josh Bray's cost protections were removed from SB 197; LG&E/KU opposed them. A Democratic tariff bill also died.
iw: No statutory cost rules

t: Kentucky offers a 50-year sales tax exemption for data center equipment
b: Passed in 2025 and championed by Senate President Robert Stivers.
iw: Very long incentive

t: Regulators approve a mandatory data center rate class for co-ops
b: EKPC's tariff requires PSC approval of each data center contract. The PSC also approved $3 billion in LG&E/KU gas plants for expected data centers.
iw: Cost rules plus new supply

t: Meta revealed behind a 1.2 GW Mason County campus
b: A think tank estimates the project could get about $50 million a year in tax breaks. Residents had objected to secrecy.
iw: Major project under scrutiny

t: Oldham County's moratorium drove off a hyperscale developer
b: The company scrapped its project after the pause; the county later extended it.
iw: Project abandoned

t: Meade County and Franklin reject data center rezonings
b: Both votes were unanimous.
iw: Projects denied

t: Memphis rejects an 18-month pause, then passes a 135-day one
b: The longer moratorium failed 6–6 after weeks of protests. The shorter pause comes with land-use standards; xAI's Colossus expansion drove the fight.
iw: Short pause in a major hub

t: Memphis mayor orders a data center rules plan within 90 days
b: Shelby County commissioners are weighing competing regulations and a 12-month moratorium.
iw: Rules coming

t: Tennessee makes big data centers pay for grid upgrades, but lets them self-power
b: Public Chapter 961 covers facilities of 50 MW and up. It also allows on-site generation or independent power producers with little state oversight.
iw: Cost rule plus freedom to self-generate

t: Tennessee bills on permits and usage reporting fail
b: Bills on registration, water permits and usage reporting, and one requiring large facilities to devote half their computing to public benefit, died in committee. The only one to pass made data centers of 50 MW or more pay for their own grid upgrades.
iw: No new state limits

t: McMinnville adopts an 18-month data center moratorium
b: Unanimous, as a 25 MW gas-and-diesel-powered project was proposed. Coffee County passed its own pause the same night.
iw: Long rural pause

t: Rutherford County planners recommend a one-year data center pause
b: The planning commission unanimously recommended a 12-month moratorium on new data center applications in unincorporated areas, doubling the six-month pause a committee backed in August. No applications are pending; it now goes to the full commission.
iw: Possible county pause

t: Montgomery County advances data center setbacks and limits
b: Approved 17–4 after raising residential setbacks from 100 to 500 feet, with limits on noise, site size and utility capacity. Because of the amendment the rules go back to the planning commission before returning in November.
iw: New siting limits

t: TVA approves up to 300 MW for xAI's Memphis operations
b: The federal utility serves most of Tennessee, which limits the state's say over rates.
iw: Power secured for a major campus

t: Mississippi permits 41 permanent gas turbines for xAI in Southaven
b: Unanimous, three weeks after a hearing where residents uniformly opposed it. Advocates appealed in April.
iw: Permanent power approved

t: NAACP sues xAI over unpermitted turbines in Southaven
b: The Clean Air Act suit seeks to stop the turbines and fines up to $124,426 a day. The state calls them temporary mobile units.
iw: Litigation over on-site power

t: Judge lets the NAACP's xAI turbine case proceed
b: The Justice Department had asked the court to dismiss it. The ruling doesn't decide whether xAI broke the law.
iw: Case survives

t: Southaven neighbors file a class action over turbine noise
b: Three residents sued xAI, SpaceX and MZX Tech in federal court over gas turbines powering the Colossus data centers, citing near-constant noise and vibration. MZX later offered to buy nearby homes in exchange for releases.
iw: Nuisance litigation

t: State sets a schedule to retire xAI's 69 temporary turbines
b: Retirements begin Aug. 18, but some units can run until July 2027.
iw: Phase-out with extensions

t: Southaven approves another SpaceXAI data center
b: The company's fifth in the Memphis area.
iw: Project approved

t: Jackson pauses data center approvals
b: Covers a 230-acre Saxum proposal, with an airport-area exception.
iw: Capital city pause

t: Mississippi's Amazon law gives data centers sweeping breaks
b: Passed in two days: large tax breaks, eased utility permitting and confidential negotiated rates.
iw: Strong incentives

t: Alabama's data center cost law takes effect
b: Act 2026-610 requires regulators to find that contracts for data centers of 150 MW and up cover their full cost and benefit other customers.
iw: Cost test for big contracts

t: Alabama regulators must vote publicly on big data center contracts
b: A vote is due within 90 days or the contract is deemed approved. Alabama Power must publish summaries; earlier filings redacted key terms.
iw: More scrutiny of deals

t: Bessemer rezones about 700 acres for 1,200 MW Project Marvel
b: Approved 5–2 for a QTS campus; the mayor and city attorney had signed nondisclosure agreements.
iw: Huge campus approved

t: Two Bessemer council members who backed Project Marvel lose their seats
b: A third was forced into a runoff and the mayor, who signed an NDA, faces one too.
iw: Voters punish approvals

t: Birmingham pauses data centers over 20 MW for six months
b: Unanimous. Applications already under review, including Nebius's AI factory in Oxmoor Valley and a DC Blox expansion, are exempt. Zoning rules passed in June take effect when the pause ends.
iw: Big-city pause

t: Homewood, Cullman, Leeds and Fort Payne pause data centers
b: Springville and Morgan County followed in June and July.
iw: Local pauses spreading

t: Alabama counties oppose data-center-only zoning power and seek broader authority
b: The county commissions association voted unanimously against zoning power limited to one industry and asked for a broader look at county land-use authority. Most of the 67 counties can't zone, so they can't pause data centers.
iw: Push for local control

t: Georgia Power can charge big data centers for upstream grid costs
b: The rule covers new customers over 100 MW. Kemp has cited it in opposing new statutes.
iw: Higher connection costs

t: Regulators approve nearly 10,000 MW of new plants for data center growth
b: About 80% is expected to serve data centers.
iw: Supply for new campuses

t: Kemp vetoed a two-year pause on data center tax breaks
b: HB 1192 would have suspended the sales tax exemption. The breaks remain.
iw: Incentive preserved

t: Georgia's data center sales tax exemption now costs a projected $2.5B a year
b: Created in 2018 and running through 2031, the estimate is up 664% from an earlier $327 million.
iw: Large incentive in force

t: Senate votes 32–21 to repeal data center tax breaks; House never acts
b: SB 410 from Sen. Matt Brass died without a House hearing.
iw: Repeal failed

t: House passes a data center cost-shield bill 159–5; it doesn't become law
b: Critics said HB 1063 mostly codified the PSC's existing rule.
iw: Status quo holds

t: Bills for 2027 include a statewide pause and an end to tax breaks
b: One would pause construction through 2028; others would repeal or move up the exemption's expiration.
iw: Renewed pressure in 2027

t: Bulloch County rejects an outright ban 4–3 but keeps its pause
b: Chairman David Bennett broke a 3–3 tie against the ban. The moratorium still runs through Dec. 31, and commissioners formed a 21-member citizen working group on regulations.
iw: Pause continues

t: DeKalb extends its data center moratorium again
b: In place since July 2025, it was extended 5–2 for 100 days, through Sept. 30. On June 23 the board rejected the county's draft data center rules.
iw: Repeated extensions

t: Augusta extends its pause, but QTS's campus stays exempt
b: Unanimous. The 49-day June pause was extended 60 days with three public hearings, and the QTS campus already under construction stays exempt. In October the commission adopted permanent rules 6–5.
iw: Pause with a big carve-out

t: Duke, regulators' staff and tech giants settle on a large-load tariff
b: Would cover customers of 50 MW and up at high load factors, or 150 MW at any. Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Meta signed; it needs NCUC approval.
iw: Upfront connection costs

t: Regulators deny a Duke gas turbine, citing uncertain data center demand
b: Voted 2–1 against the 255 MW unit at Hamlet, calling its costs certain and its need uncertain.
iw: Supply buildout slowed

t: Charlotte adopts a 150-day data center moratorium
b: Voted 11–0; it runs through Nov. 5. Projects already approved, including the PowerHouse campus under construction, are exempt under state law.
iw: Big-city pause

t: Charlotte votes Oct. 26 on extending its moratorium to October 2027
b: The 150-day pause expires Nov. 5. Staff and a task force recommend extending it up to 11 months after a survey found 78% of respondents opposed; unions urged the council to let it lapse.
iw: Likely extension

t: Raleigh pauses approvals for data centers over 5 MW
b: Voted 7–1 for a six-month pause on major data centers; facilities of 10,000 sq ft or less drawing 5 MW or less are exempt. It runs to April 6, 2027. Advocates wanted 32 months, and the vote followed a withdrawn proposal on Jones Sausage Road.
iw: Capital city pause

t: Forsyth County rejects a six-month moratorium
b: Voted 5–2 after the county attorney warned of litigation, citing a developer's win against Chatham County's pause. Commissioner Dan Besse, who drafted it, said it would apply only to new proposals.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Forsyth denies a Rural Hall data center rezoning 5–2
b: The vote applied to the Rural Hall-area application only and did not bar data centers generally.
iw: Project denied

t: Greensboro pauses data centers over 10 MW for 180 days
b: Voted 8–0 with one recusal; it runs through Feb. 14, 2027. The council lengthened it from 120 days after public comment, and permitted projects are exempt.
iw: City pause

t: Alamance County adopts a one-year pause on 10 MW projects
b: Unanimous, for unincorporated areas. It grew from a six-month proposal after more than 23 residents spoke in favor.
iw: County pause

t: Durham County pauses large data centers through May 2027
b: Voted 4–1, aligning with the city. Facilities under 100,000 sq ft with closed-loop cooling and no diesel generators are exempt; Commissioner Nida Allam voted no over that carve-out.
iw: Nine-month pause

t: Statesville and Waxhaw adopt data center pauses
b: Statesville's unanimous 180-day pause took effect Sept. 14 and exempts the approved Compass campus on Stamey Farm Road. Waxhaw unanimously adopted 12 months on Aug. 11 with no proposal pending.
iw: Town pauses

t: Mountain counties and towns pause data centers
b: Clay, Madison, Swain and Watauga counties and Boone, Brevard, Clyde, Canton and Hendersonville have adopted moratoriums.
iw: Regional wave

t: Chatham County's moratorium stands, but a judge exempts Eco TIP's 750 MW project
b: The February pause runs to Feb. 11, 2027. A judge granted Eco TIP West summary judgment, letting its $11 million Moncure project proceed and leaving the county open to damages.
iw: Court limits local pauses

t: Stokes County rejects a data center pause, 3–2
b: Commissioners overrode their planning board's call for a six-month moratorium and adopted data center rules instead. They later approved the Project Delta rezoning on Sept. 14, again 3–2.
iw: Pauses rejected

t: Lee County permits a 90 MW CyrusOne data center
b: The Sanford-Lee County planning department issued a construction permit for the 300,000 sq ft first phase on Lower Moncure Road, developed by PointOne and Helix Ventures and to be owned by CyrusOne. Residents had demanded a pause; commissioners have not adopted one.
iw: Project proceeds

t: Datacenter Transparency Act would pause siting permits for two years
b: Covers facilities of 100 MW and up from August 2026 to August 2028; referred to the Rules Committee.
iw: Statewide pause proposal

t: Boone, Iowa, approves Lightedge's data center site plan and a water cap
b: The council approved a site plan for two 125,000 sq ft colocation buildings and an agreement capping water use at 75,000 gallons a month with no city tax incentives. Lightedge came to Boone after Ames delayed its decision to May 2027; Boone isn't final among its sites.
iw: Local welcome

t: South Carolina's 2025 energy law adds data center ratepayer protections
b: Meant to keep data center costs off other customers.
iw: Cost protections

t: South Carolina's data center permitting and moratorium bills die
b: S.867 and S.902 never reached a floor vote, and moratorium bills H.5526 and H.5286 stalled.
iw: No state rules

t: Spartanburg County freezes data centers over 65 MW for a year
b: Passed 5–1; the Valara project already approved is unaffected.
iw: County pause with a high threshold

t: Self-powered Spartanburg data center isn't subject to power plant rules
b: The ruling covers the $2.8 billion project at a former Kohler plant.
iw: Lighter rules for self-power

t: TigerDC withdraws its Spartanburg incentive request after pushback
b: Residents had opposed property tax breaks for the project.
iw: Project withdrawn

t: Settlement bans data centers in most of Colleton's ACE Basin
b: Resolves a lawsuit over a 1,000 MW, 859-acre proposal. The county had adopted a six-month moratorium in July.
iw: Large area closed to data centers

t: Chesterfield and Newberry counties pause data centers
b: Newberry first voted down a land sale to a developer; Greenwood County began its own 12-month pause.
iw: County pauses

t: Florida utilities file data center rates under the new state law
b: FPL says its rates already comply, with 20-year contracts and full payment for new generation. Tampa Electric filed a new tariff; Duke's is under review.
iw: Strict cost terms

t: Florida's 2025 tax package limits the data center sales tax break to 100 MW-plus sites
b: HB 7031 extended the exemption's application window by 10 years but, from Aug. 1, 2025, limited it to data centers with at least 100 MW of IT load, ending it for smaller facilities.
iw: Incentive reduced

t: 68% of Florida voters oppose an AI data center in their community
b: Only 28% support one, with energy, bills, noise and water the top concerns.
iw: Strong opposition

t: Donalds favors local approvals with strict protections
b: His Democratic opponent, David Jolly, pledges a statewide one-year moratorium.
iw: Conditional support

t: Volusia County bans data centers of 50 MW or more
b: Applies in unincorporated areas, citing the aquifer and sinkholes. Smaller projects face extra review.
iw: Permanent county ban

t: Broward County moves toward a one-year moratorium
b: Unanimous vote to begin the process for unincorporated areas.
iw: Likely county pause

t: Wakulla County bans data centers outright
b: Unanimous, for unincorporated areas. Staff said zoning already excluded data centers; the ordinance makes it explicit.
iw: County ban

t: North Port adopts an 18-month data center moratorium
b: Passed 3–2. A pending 896,000 sq ft application can keep moving through review but can't get final approval during the pause; the two no votes wanted it stopped outright.
iw: Long city pause

t: Marion County pauses data centers of 50 MW or more for a year
b: Approved 4–1, then adopted 5–0. Commissioner Kathy Bryant dissented because she wanted smaller facilities covered too.
iw: County pause

t: Edgewater enacts a permanent ban on data centers and crypto mining
b: Unanimous, ahead of a Nov. 3 vote to write it into the city charter.
iw: Permanent city ban

t: Levy and Putnam counties pause large data centers
b: Levy's moratorium runs Oct. 1 to Sept. 30, 2027, citing reliance on the Floridan Aquifer.
iw: County pauses

t: Sarasota County and Lakeland adopt one-year pauses
b: Sarasota County voted 5–0 on July 8 to pause hyperscale projects until July 2027. Lakeland's 4–3 vote on Aug. 3 covers users of 50 MW or more, including sites outside the city seeking its utilities.
iw: Local pauses

t: Clay, Hernando and Lake counties adopt one-year moratoriums
b: Approved the same day.
iw: County pauses

t: Jackson County pauses AI data centers before any are proposed
b: Unanimous, with no project proposed. On June 9 the board rescinded it in favor of an outright ban, adopted June 23.
iw: Preemptive county pause

t: Tallahassee rejects a data center moratorium 3–2
b: The city manager said the comprehensive plan and zoning already keep data centers out. Commissioner Jeremy Matlow, who proposed the pause, disputed that reading.
iw: Ban rejected, zoning already restrictive

t: Indiantown rejects a data center pause 4–1 pending new legal advice
b: Council members wanted new counsel to vet the language after the village attorney resigned. They fired the village manager the same night.
iw: Pauses rejected

t: Escambia County bans large data centers and drops a separate moratorium
b: A July resolution declared data centers not a permitted use, and an Aug. 6 ordinance, passed 4–1, banned large-scale ones in unincorporated areas. In September the board took no action on a moratorium, saying they were already banned.
iw: County ban

t: Louisiana offers 20-year data center sales tax relief
b: Act 730 sets a low bar of $200 million and 50 jobs, stacked with parish deals.
iw: Generous incentive

t: Regulators approve three gas plants for Meta's Hyperion campus
b: Built for Meta in Richland Parish over substantial community pushback.
iw: Dedicated supply approved

t: Louisiana fast-tracks power plants for large loads
b: An executive order led regulators to adopt the Lightning Amendment, which skips the usual least-cost review.
iw: Faster approvals

t: Regulators fast-track seven more gas plants for Meta's expansion
b: About 5.3 GW in Richland and Pointe Coupee parishes. A consumer group estimates data center growth could add $26 billion in system costs.
iw: More supply likely

t: Regulators vote 3–1 to keep Meta's data center details secret
b: Overturned a judge's subpoena for how Meta calculated its jobs and power needs. The vote split along party lines.
iw: Less disclosure

t: Entergy discloses Meta will use 4,500 MW as hearing opens
b: Entergy has a settlement with regulators' staff; opponents say ratepayers could be left with plant costs after Meta's 20-year contract.
iw: Approval expected

t: Landry says Louisiana doesn't need a moratorium
b: He favors what he calls responsible growth as other states clamp down.
iw: Pro-development stance

t: New Orleans bars data centers until mid-2027
b: An interim zoning ban; Caddo Parish has twice rejected a pause.
iw: City ban

t: Two Louisiana PSC seats are on the ballot
b: The commission will rule on Hyperion's second phase and large-load tariff policy.
iw: Regulator makeup at stake

t: Arkansas's Act 851 limits how cities can restrict data centers
b: Written mostly for crypto mining; Little Rock's mayor says it means cities can't ban data centers.
iw: Limits local bans

t: Little Rock adopts data center zoning rules
b: Defines hyperscale as over 250,000 square feet or 75 MW. Residents wanted a moratorium on a proposed Google project.
iw: Rules, not a pause

t: Little Rock rejects a data center moratorium on a 4–4 tie again
b: A six-month pause failed by the same vote as an 18-month one in August.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Pulaski County rejects a 12-month moratorium
b: Voted 10–3 with one present. Justices also rejected, 8–6, an amendment exempting the first phase of AVAIO Digital's Wrightsville project.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Pulaski County judge vetoes data center rules
b: The quorum court passed conditional-use rules 11–4. Hyde cited legal and financial risk to the county; an override needs nine of 15 votes.
iw: Rules blocked for now

t: Pulaski County may vote to override the veto
b: The rules would require conditional use permits, setbacks and noise caps with no AVAIO carve-out.
iw: Possible new rules

t: Independence County adopts a five-year moratorium
b: Runs through Aug. 31, 2031, citing water supply strain; no project had been proposed.
iw: Very long pause

t: Madison County adopts a three-year moratorium
b: Voted 8–0 for a pause through Aug. 31, 2029. Union and Carroll counties adopted one-year pauses in June and Russellville six months in July.
iw: Long pause

t: Lawmakers grill Entergy over charging ratepayers for Google-linked solar
b: A rider covers Cypress Solar for Google's West Memphis campus. A judge rejected Entergy's bid to stop a newspaper publishing its Google agreements.
iw: Scrutiny of cost shifting

t: Woodford County becomes the first Kentucky county to ban data centers permanently
b: The unanimous vote was tied to farmland preservation and local opposition, with the judge-executive pointing to a fight in neighboring Mercer County as a warning.
iw: Permanent county ban

t: TVA creates a data center rate class with higher rates and upfront commitments
b: Approved at a Memphis board meeting, it raises data center rates about 10% on average over three years and requires capacity commitments to fund transmission and connections, so households don't foot the bill.
iw: Higher rates for big users

t: Louisville adopts a six-month pause on new data center applications
b: The pause covers specified rezoning, conditional-use and development-plan applications while the city writes rules, amid opposition to a planned hyperscale facility in West Louisville.
iw: Six-month city pause

t: Knoxville pauses large data centers for a year
b: The emergency ordinance halts permits and construction for data centers needing 10 MW or more while planners write zoning rules, since the city code doesn't define the use.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Knox County adopts a one-year data center moratorium, 10–0
b: The pause runs through June 30, 2027, or until the county adopts data center rules. Knoxville followed with its own pause in July.
iw: One-year county pause

t: Anderson, Morgan and Loudon counties pause data centers; Blount sets strict rules
b: Anderson and Morgan adopted two-year pauses and Loudon a six-month one. Blount limits data centers to industrial zones, 5,000 feet from homes, schools and churches, with a 60-decibel cap.
iw: Regional wave of limits

t: Mason County rezones about 2,080 acres for a proposed data center campus
b: The vote moved 28 properties north of Germantown Road to rural industrial zoning for an unnamed company's six-building campus. In October the county approved a development agreement with Meta, revealed as the user.
iw: Land cleared for a large campus

w: NAACP, Young, Gifted & Green and Safe and Sound Coalition
t: Groups appeal Mississippi's permit for 41 xAI turbines in Southaven
b: SELC filed the appeal of the March 10 permit, which does not cover the temporary turbines already running at the site.
iw: Permit under challenge

t: Alabama cuts new data center tax breaks to 20 years
b: HB 399 caps abatements granted from 2027 at 20 years unless operators sign community investment deals, and makes 100 MW-plus sites pay state sales and non-school property taxes once open.
iw: Smaller tax breaks

t: Bessemer rezones 914 more acres, expanding Project Marvel to about 1,600
b: QTS, owned by Blackstone funds, later confirmed it is behind the 18-building, 1,200 MW campus. The extra land is for wider buffers and layout flexibility.
iw: Larger campus approved

t: Clarksdale conditionally rezones 648 acres for a possible hyperscale campus
b: Conditions include a $5 million impact fee, water caps and a 1,000-foot residential buffer. No developer has been named, and residents have challenged the notice process in court.
iw: Land readied for a campus

t: Bill to end a Mississippi data center income tax break dies
b: HB 4045 would have ended the income tax exemption for certain data center projects after 2026 and created a development fund tied to large fee-in-lieu deals. It died on the House calendar.
iw: Incentives unchanged

t: Hundreds pack a Southaven hearing; every speaker opposes xAI's turbine permit
b: Residents described health problems and constant noise they blame on the plant during the hearing on 41 permanent turbines, which regulators approved weeks later.
iw: Organized opposition

t: Meade County adopts a 12-month data center moratorium
b: The ordinance pauses permits and site plans for data centers while the county updates its zoning and comprehensive plan. It followed the county's October rejection of a 138-acre data center rezoning.
iw: One-year county pause

t: Sweetwater limits data centers to heavy industrial zones with a 60-decibel cap
b: The ordinance also requires five-acre lots and setbacks of 150 to 200 feet, rising to 500 feet next to homes.
iw: Strict local rules

t: Two Alabama utility commissioners lose GOP primaries amid anger over power bills
b: Jeremy Oden and Chip Beeker lost after widespread outcry over high electric bills, as data centers became a top election issue. Only Cynthia Almond will keep her seat next year.
iw: Pressure on regulators

t: Memphis pollution board dismisses the appeal of xAI's turbine permit, 6–1
b: SELC's July appeal argued the permit ignored xAI's unpermitted turbines and misread the Clean Air Act. The board found the case moot because most turbines had been removed.
iw: Permit stands

t: Alabama freezes power rates through 2027 and approves solar for a Meta data center
b: The 3–0 vote delayed the Lindsay Hill gas plant charge to 2028 and approved two Baldwin County solar farms serving Meta. Critics said the freeze postpones costs rather than avoiding them.
iw: Rates frozen, data center supply added

t: Residents rally against Project Marvel days before Bessemer's rezoning vote
b: Speakers at the Legacy YMCA cited noise, diesel generator pollution, heavy water use and a rare fish, the Birmingham darter, and said officials hadn't answered their questions.
iw: Organized opposition

t: Kentucky regulators let LG&E/KU build $3 billion in gas plants for data centers
b: The PSC approved two new units for an expected 1,470 MW of load growth but rejected a special cost-recovery mechanism and barred construction if the forecast demand doesn't materialize.
iw: Supply added with safeguards

t: Memphis steers 25% of xAI's property taxes to nearby neighborhoods
b: The ordinance covers both Colossus sites and a planned water recycling plant, capped at $100 million for projects within five miles. A bid to raise the share to 75% failed.
iw: Community benefit, no new limits

t: Advocates rally at Kentucky PSC as LG&E/KU seeks gas plants for data centers
b: Outside the hearing, critics said the proposed tariff for 100 MW-plus users, which requires paying for 80% of contracted energy for 15 years, only protects customers if the data centers get built.
iw: Pushback on utility plans

t: Mississippi lets xAI run temporary gas turbines in Southaven without permits
b: After an xAI affiliate bought a former Duke Energy plant in July, regulators treated its turbines for Colossus 2 as exempt temporary units. The count reached 27 by December, and neighbors complained of noise.
iw: Power without permits

t: Regulators let Alabama Power buy a $622 million gas plant for data center demand
b: The Lindsay Hill plant in Autauga County was bought to meet growth driven largely by data centers. A later rate freeze pushed the roughly $3.32 monthly customer charge for it to 2028.
iw: Supply added for data centers

t: Shelby County permits 15 gas turbines at xAI's Memphis data center
b: xAI had installed as many as 35 turbines without permits over the prior year. The department also ruled that temporary turbines need no permit, a stance critics said opened a loophole.
iw: Permanent on-site power approved

t: Residents' lawsuit briefly halts Bessemer's Project Marvel rezoning
b: A judge's April order blocked a council vote over inadequate public notice, and the city restarted the process. The council approved the rezoning in November, and the suit was later dismissed.
iw: Challenge ended

t: Bessemer officials sign a secrecy agreement with Project Marvel's developer
b: The mayor, city attorney and chief of staff agreed not to share developer names, site plans or studies. The city released the agreement in July 2026 after environmental groups threatened to sue.
iw: Secrecy shields the developer

t: Mississippi offers tax breaks for Compass's $10 billion Meridian campus
b: State certification brings 10-year income and franchise tax exemptions and sales tax breaks on construction materials and equipment, plus a $4 million legislative site grant. Mississippi Power will supply about 500 MW.
iw: State incentives for a hyperscale campus

t: Control of Georgia's utility regulator is on the Nov. 3 ballot
b: Hubbard faces Fitz Johnson again, and two newcomers vie for a second seat; Democratic wins in both would flip the commission to a 3–2 majority. Candidates in both parties say data centers must pay their own way.
iw: Could reshape data center rate decisions

t: Staff approval nearly triples data center space at the Project Tango site
b: Using existing master-plan rights, the county's Development Review Officer raised allowed data center space from about 200,000 to nearly 700,000 sq ft, weeks after commissioners adopted a moratorium.
iw: Project advances despite the pause

t: Moore says he would sign a statewide data center moratorium
b: He told Punchbowl News he would sign a moratorium or ban if lawmakers sent one, a week after his campaign declined to say whether he supported a pause.
iw: Statewide pause now possible

t: Frederick County rejects a development agreement for the Frederick Digital Campus
b: Fitzwater also extended the county's pause on new data center applications to July 1, 2027. The campus is Maryland's only approved hyperscale project.
iw: Setback for the state's only hyperscale campus

t: Delaware makes data centers pay their own grid costs under PSC-approved contracts
b: HB 233 requires facilities of 50 MW or more to win commission approval of service agreements of at least 10 years and bars hookups until a separate rate class exists. Data centers without their own power would be cut first in a blackout.
iw: Full-cost contracts required

t: Delaware requires big data centers to supply their own power within 10 years
b: HB 445 makes large energy users generate or secure all the electricity they use; those that can't at the start must follow a ramp-up plan reaching 100% within a decade.
iw: Bring-your-own-power mandate

t: Delaware bars new data centers from job-based tax credits
b: HB 310 keeps new large-load facilities from claiming state tax incentives tied to the jobs they create.
iw: Loss of job tax credits

t: Montgomery County passes an 18-month moratorium and blocks data centers over 25 MW
b: The unanimous vote codifies and extends Elrich's six-month June order and covers the proposed Dickerson campus at a retired coal plant, whose developer had appealed the executive order.
iw: Long pause plus a size cap

t: Palm Beach County rejects the Project Tango AI campus, 5–1
b: After a 12-hour hearing, commissioners denied without prejudice a bid to expand the Loxahatchee site to 3.6 million sq ft near homes and an elementary school. The developer has sued.
iw: Hyperscale expansion rejected

t: Prince George's adopts a two-year pause on hyperscale data centers
b: Passed 7–1 with three abstentions. It bars planning review of hyperscale applications and ends early if the council adopts comprehensive data center legislation.
iw: Two-year county pause

t: York County pauses new data centers for nine months, but QTS's campus is exempt
b: Unanimous vote for a pause running into April 2027. QTS's nine site plans near Lake Wylie were approved earlier, so the county treats them as vested.
iw: Pause with a big exemption

t: Howard County halts new data centers through November 2027
b: The council unanimously passed CB31-2026, the S.M.A.R.T. Siting Act, which also creates a task force of up to 11 members to study impacts.
iw: County pause into late 2027

t: Stream cancels its Marion County data center, citing too little power
b: The developer said it could not secure enough electricity for the planned campus.
iw: Power shortage stops a project

t: Utility RELIEF Act widens Maryland's data center tariff and creates a registry
b: The law lowers the large-load threshold to 25 MW at 60% utilization, makes data centers pay for their grid upgrades and PJM-assigned capacity costs, and requires them to register with the PSC and disclose water and power plans.
iw: Wider cost rules and disclosure

t: New Castle County adopts its first data center zoning rules, 12–0
b: Data centers are limited to industrial zones, need 1,000-foot setbacks from homes unless a noise study allows 500, must meet a 55 dB(A) noise cap and can't use open-loop cooling without reclaimed water. Projects already filed are exempt.
iw: New limits, but not on pending projects

t: Tucker County groups lose their appeal of the Ridgeline power plant permit
b: The Air Quality Board upheld the permit but required continued air monitoring. In August an appeals court ruled it lacked jurisdiction, leaving a possible state Supreme Court appeal.
iw: Permit stands for now

t: Delaware rules half of Project Washington violates the Coastal Zone Act
b: Regulators cited 516 diesel backup generators and the risk of fuel spills into the Delaware River and Bay. The Coastal Zone Industrial Control Board upheld the decision in late March.
iw: Blocks the state's largest proposal

t: Lawmakers override Moore's veto of a state data center impact study
b: Moore vetoed the study in May 2025; the Senate overrode him 44–0 and the House 109–21 in a December special session. The report, due Sept. 1, 2026, was still overdue weeks later.
iw: Study, not rules

t: About 400 turn out against a 1,000 MW data center near the ACE Basin
b: Eagle Rock Partners' proposal followed a November rule change letting the zoning board approve data centers in one vote. The developer didn't reapply, and residents sued over the rule.
iw: Opposition stalled the project

t: Virginia regulators create a data center rate class with 14-year contracts
b: Starting in 2027, Dominion customers of 25 MW or more must pay at least 85% of contracted transmission and distribution demand and 60% of generation demand, post collateral and owe exit fees if they leave early.
iw: Minimum bills for big users

t: Florida regulators approve FPL's large-load tariffs for data centers
b: The 2026–2029 rate deal makes data centers fund new generation and substations, post collateral and sign 20-year contracts with minimum bills. A developers' group had warned FPL's first version would drive projects out of its territory.
iw: Data centers fund their own generation

t: Democrats flip two Georgia PSC seats amid anger over power bills
b: Alicia Johnson and Peter Hubbard won about 63% each, the party's first non-federal statewide wins in nearly 20 years. Hubbard had published an analysis arguing data center rate discounts shift costs onto households.
iw: Tougher regulators on costs

t: Edgecombe County writes data centers into its zoning code after Tarboro's rejection
b: Commissioners updated the county's Unified Development Ordinance on Nov. 3 to cover data centers.
iw: New local rules

t: Delaware regulators pause new large-load hookups while they write a tariff
b: Acting on a Sept. 3 petition from the Public Advocate and commission staff, the PSC opened a large-load tariff docket and paused interconnection of new large loads such as data centers in Delmarva Power's territory.
iw: Utility-wide pause on new large loads

t: Project Washington's developer signs a union labor deal ahead of county hearings
b: The agreement with 20 local building trades unions gave Starwood a key ally as New Castle County weighed new data center rules and a rezoning the project still needs.
iw: Labor support for the project

t: Prince George's County pauses data center permits for 180 days
b: CR-98-2025 froze permits and subdivision plans while a county task force weighed costs and benefits, alongside an executive order from County Executive Aisha Braveboy. The county adopted a longer pause in 2026.
iw: Six-month county pause

t: Statesville rezones 330 acres for a Compass data center campus, 8–0
b: The council approved the farmland rezoning despite neighborhood opposition, in what backers called the largest potential private investment in Iredell County. A year later the city paused new data centers.
iw: Large campus approved

t: Tarboro rejects a 300 MW data center, 6–1
b: The 52-acre plan included on-site generation and battery storage. Energy Storage Solutions sued, then settled in 2026 and said it would not build in Tarboro.
iw: Project rejected and abandoned

w: Pike, Lamar, Troup and Clayton counties
t: Pike, Lamar, Troup and Clayton counties and LaGrange pause data centers
b: The September wave brought Georgia to eight local moratoriums since March. Lamar acted after Amazon Web Services bought 985 acres there for $270 million.
iw: Wave of local pauses

t: West Virginia approves the air permit for Tucker County's Ridgeline power plant
b: The DEP classified Fundamental Data's off-grid gas plant as a minor source despite more than 1,600 mostly opposed comments, and let parts of the application stay confidential.
iw: Power plant cleared to proceed

t: Gov. Meyer calls the 1.2 GW Delaware City data center a nonstarter
b: Starwood Digital Ventures' Project Washington would cover about 6 million sq ft near Delaware City and draw about 1.2 GW. Meyer said he would do everything he could to keep so large a power user out of the state.
iw: Governor opposes the state's biggest proposal

t: DeKalb County adopts a 100-day data center moratorium, 4–3
b: Planning staff had told developers data centers were allowed on some light-industrial sites. The board extended the pause in December and again in 2026, and a developer has sued.
iw: County pause, repeatedly extended

t: Youngkin vetoes Virginia's data center site assessment bill
b: HB 1601 and SB 1449 would have required noise studies within 500 feet of homes and schools for 100 MW projects and let localities demand reviews of effects on water, farmland, parks, historic sites and forests.
iw: No new state review requirements

t: Maryland's Next Generation Energy Act creates a large-load tariff for data centers
b: New users of 100 MW or more at 80% utilization must pay a separate tariff covering the grid costs they impose. The 2026 RELIEF Act later widened it to smaller data centers.
iw: Separate rates for big users

t: Coweta County pauses data centers for 180 days after approving Project Peach
b: Weeks after a 3–2 vote rezoned 320 acres for the $1 billion Project Peach, commissioners paused new projects as a $17 billion Project Sail drew a 1,750-signature petition.
iw: Six-month county pause

t: About 300 pack a Davis meeting on Tucker County's data center power plant
b: Residents of the tourism towns of Davis and Thomas, blindsided by Fundamental Data's plan that March, pressed for details on pollution, noise and the end use of the power.
iw: Organized local opposition

t: Loudoun ends by-right approval for new data centers
b: The 7–2 vote requires a special exception with public hearings for every new data center. A separate 5–4 resolution grandfathered applications filed before Feb. 12 that sit more than 500 feet from homes.
iw: Every new project needs a public vote

t: Douglas County adopts a 90-day data center moratorium
b: Metro Atlanta's first pause responded to a cluster of pending data center projects.
iw: Short county pause

t: Atlanta bars new data centers from the BeltLine overlay district
b: Council members cited soaring data center growth, energy use of up to 730 MW and water scarcity when they barred the facilities from the 22-mile BeltLine area.
iw: Ban in the city's core

t: Maryland eases permitting for data center backup generators
b: Moore predicted at the May 2024 signing that the Critical Infrastructure Streamlining Act would give the industry a major boost in Maryland.
iw: Faster generator approvals

t: Maryland's 2020 sales tax exemption for data center equipment stays in place
b: SB 397 passed 45–0 and 123–6 and took effect without Gov. Hogan's signature. A 2026 repeal bill, HB 560, drew 21 Democratic sponsors and a hearing but no committee vote.
iw: Valuable tax break survives a repeal push

t: Fayetteville schedules a hearing on a data center moratorium after a 6–4 vote
b: The divided council also voted to keep drafting regulations; the city has debated the issue for months, and Cumberland County's pause does not cover city limits.
iw: Pause under consideration

t: Stafford approves the Accokeek Center data center campus, 4–3
b: The rezoning allows about 590,000 sq ft on 121 acres with roughly $6.4 million in developer contributions and limits on water use, despite a crowd opposed to the project.
iw: Campus approved with conditions

t: Spanberger's energy plan asks data centers to cover the cost increases they cause
b: The long-term plan, unveiled with her budget, also leans on solar and storage and needs legislation in 2027; Republicans said it would raise costs.
iw: Proposed cost shift to data centers

t: Virginia cites Google's first Chesterfield data center site for seven runoff violations
b: The notice documents sediment discharges between December 2025 and August 2026 affecting thousands of feet of stream channel and about 1.4 acres of wetlands; Google blamed heavy rain.
iw: Enforcement underway

t: Lovejoy bans data centers citywide
b: The ban came after Stillwater Development withdrew its 3.5 million sq ft, 1.25 GW campus near two schools in August. The ordinance also repealed a permit path that could have allowed data centers.
iw: Citywide ban

t: Virginia proposes a record $2.5 million penalty for a Microsoft data center
b: A June 2025 substation failure left the Leesburg site running 62 diesel generators for a week, pushing it past permit limits. Microsoft agreed to fund expanded air monitoring; public comment closed Oct. 14.
iw: Costly generator limits

t: Holly Springs, Spring Hope, Boiling Spring Lakes, Hillsborough and Southport pause data centers
b: Spring Hope acted in May; Holly Springs, Boiling Spring Lakes and Hillsborough in June; and Southport on Sept. 10 with no project proposed.
iw: More local pauses

t: Marietta, Walker County and Forest Park adopt data center pauses
b: Marietta's July 8 pause runs through Dec. 31 but didn't cover a pending 18 MW project approved 5–2 in August. Walker County's 30-day July pause was extended 180 days Aug. 6, and Forest Park approved 90 days Aug. 31.
iw: More local pauses

t: Mercer County rejects rules that would have allowed hyperscale data centers
b: The unanimous voice vote blocked siting next to a coal plant near Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill; nearby Burgin is weighing annexation for a hyperscale project.
iw: Hyperscale siting blocked

t: Senator's poll finds 55% of his Madison County district oppose more data centers
b: Givhan's survey of his Huntsville-area district came as north Alabama debates new data centers under TVA's new data center rates.
iw: Local opposition measured

t: Calvert County pauses data center site plans after Amazon drops its project
b: Amazon withdrew its Calvert Technology Center plan in early August following voter backlash in the June primary; the six-month moratorium took effect Aug. 28.
iw: Six-month county pause

t: Cary adopts an 18-month data center pause
b: Staff will study power demand, water use, noise and site design, with the council expected to revisit the issue in February 2028.
iw: 18-month town pause

t: Asheville, Woodfin, Franklin and Jackson County pause data centers
b: Woodfin acted in May, Asheville unanimously in June, Franklin in July and Jackson County on Aug. 18, each for about a year.
iw: Regional wave of pauses

t: Alabama Power files data center contracts with key terms blacked out
b: Filings for Meta- and Nebius-linked projects hide contract length, power amounts, prices and minimum bills, though the utility says each deal covers its own costs.
iw: Secrecy over terms

t: Kent County adopts data center rules with a 55-decibel cap, 7–0
b: The ordinance limits where facilities can go, requires plans for water, power, cooling and cleanup, and orders removal within 180 days after a year of disuse.
iw: New county limits

t: Douglas County rejects a 4.4 million sq ft campus near Villa Rica, 4–1
b: The EdgeConneX-linked plan for about 700 acres had shrunk from an earlier 11-building proposal; the planning commission recommended denial and residents played noise demonstrations.
iw: Project rejected

t: Boyd and Greenup counties pause data centers but exempt the Muskie campus
b: Both six-month moratoriums exclude EastPark Industrial Park, where TeraWulf plans a campus of more than 1 GW. Boyd's judge-executive said exempting the park would otherwise impose on its other member counties.
iw: More local pauses

t: Bowling Green adopts data center standards after rejecting a moratorium
b: Ordinance BG2026-6 sets rules on energy and water demand, noise, light, setbacks and site design.
iw: New city rules

t: Cumberland County pauses data centers for six months, 7–0
b: The ban on site plan reviews and permits runs to Dec. 15 while staff write rules on water, power, noise and distance from homes, schools and Fort Bragg.
iw: Six-month county pause

t: Durham extends its data center pause to a full year
b: The council first passed a 60-day moratorium on May 4, then unanimously added 10 months; Durham County later matched it through May 2027.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Hundreds of thousands sign a petition against a data center near the Nashville Zoo
b: More than 150 people also spoke against proposals near the zoo and Fisk University at a June planning meeting, before the city paused data center permits.
iw: Mass opposition

t: Daviess County adopts a 12-month data center moratorium
b: Residents pushed for the pause after news of a hyperscale project planned at an idled aluminum mill in neighboring Hancock County.
iw: One-year county pause

t: Cave City pauses data centers for a year; a developer sues
b: Kentucky Industrial Alliance, which had filed plans for 318 acres, sued June 8; the Kentucky League of Cities is helping fund the city's defense.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Harnett County adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: The pause came amid a Triangle-area wave that also reached Cumberland, Durham and Wake County towns.
iw: One-year county pause

t: Citrus County pauses data centers for a year; Deltona later drops its 800-acre plan
b: The 5–0 vote covers data center rezonings and permits. Deltona withdrew its Holder Industrial Park applications in June after the planning commission rejected the land-use change.
iw: One-year county pause

t: Simpson County's top official backs a statewide data center moratorium
b: Barnes said no Kentucky community is ready for a data center as his county fights TenKey's project in court.
iw: Local official seeks state pause

t: Vance County rezones land along U.S. 158 for a possible Natelli data center
b: Natelli later filed plans for a 900 MW campus near Henderson, the state's largest active proposal.
iw: Land opened for a large campus

t: Apex adopts a one-year data center moratorium after a 250 MW plan is withdrawn
b: Natelli had pulled its New Hill Digital Campus beside the Harris nuclear plant on March 5, citing the town's zoning deliberations.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Fort Meade approves a 20-year deal for a 4.4 million sq ft hyperscale campus
b: Florida's commerce secretary called the project fundamentally flawed. Residents sued in May and started recall petitions, and the campus still needs a regional water permit.
iw: Largest Florida approval

t: Wendell pauses data centers through the end of 2026
b: The town acted with no data center proposed, citing undefined uses in its development ordinance; the pause also covers crypto mining.
iw: Town pause

t: West Virginia makes certified data centers pay county fire and ambulance fees
b: HB 5168, mainly a permanent EMS funding bill, also requires certified microgrids and high impact data centers to pay county fire and ambulance fees, and entitles them to county fire and police protection.
iw: Small new local fees

t: Appeals court upholds the voiding of the Digital Gateway rezoning
