b: Latham called off an Aug. 3 annexation and rezoning vote after its president concluded it would fail, and Logan County canceled Aug. 5-6 planning and zoning hearings because the state's attorney found technical errors in the applications. Hut 8 could resubmit for September at the earliest.
iw: Both approval paths for the biggest downstate proposal on hold

t: Residents sue to stop T5's $18 billion Grayslake data center campus
b: The Preservation of Community Well-Being Collective and nine residents sued Grayslake, T5 Data Centers and Alter Asset Management, arguing data centers are not a permitted use and closed-door deliberations violated the Open Meetings Act. They want the development agreement voided. The 473-acre, 1.2 GW campus has a building permit.
iw: Permitted hyperscale campus faces litigation over its approvals

t: Taylor County pauses data centers, solar and battery projects for a year
b: Ordinance No. 40 imposes a 12-month moratorium on new applications for data centers, solar energy systems, battery storage and mineral rights developments while the county works on regulations.
iw: Blanket pause on energy-intensive land uses

t: Turtle walks away from Panattoni's $1 billion Project Cornmaze, starts a moratorium
b: The board voted 5-0 to reject the developer's revised cost-reimbursement agreement for a 2 million-square-foot hyperscale campus straddling Turtle and the Town of Beloit, and 5-0 to begin a 12-month moratorium on developments over 10,000 square feet. The chairman reversed his early-July support; a recall petition targets him.
iw: Hyperscale campus loses its host town and faces a year-long pause

t: Pillen touts Nebraska large-load laws at White House ratepayer roundtable
b: At a White House event promoting the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, Pillen pointed to LB 1261 and LB 1010, which let public power districts set large-load rates and make data centers fund their own upgrades, and to his new task force protecting the Ogallala Aquifer.
iw: Pay-your-own-way framework paired with continued recruitment

t: Columbus pursues water and decommissioning rules instead of a moratorium
b: At a public hearing, Councilmember Christopher Wyche advanced three proposed ordinances on data center water reporting, sewer connections and closure plans, rejecting residents' calls for a ban. Special utility rates are under study. A second hearing was set for Sept. 16.
iw: Regulation rather than a ban in the state's largest city

t: Yankton County halts data center and bitcoin mining permits for six months
b: Commissioners unanimously adopted a six-month moratorium on permits for new data centers and bitcoin mining facilities, half the twelve months originally proposed, with a possible six-month extension if no ordinance is ready. Planning and zoning was told to begin drafting rules immediately.
iw: County permit freeze under the new state local-control law

t: Nodaway County enacts six-month moratorium after data center proposal surfaces
b: The unanimous order bars construction and operation of data centers and ancillary facilities in unincorporated areas, extendable six more months. Commissioners want to study grid stability, water, noise, stormwater, emergency response, tax effects and whether to adopt zoning. A developer holds a land option but has not bought the site.
iw: Pause aimed at a specific pending site

t: MISO tells FERC it will fast-track co-located generation for large loads
b: In its informational report, MISO said it remains resource adequate but promised a zero-injection interconnection agreement filing by late July and a parallel study process for large loads and their generation by late September. SPP said its existing processes already suffice.
iw: New fast lanes for bring-your-own-generation projects across MISO states

t: Walz says Pillen reversed himself on data center incentives
b: The Democratic nominee for governor said Gov. Jim Pillen had lobbied senators for data center tax incentives less than four months before his executive order barred ImagiNE Act credits for data center projects. Pillen said the order is not a moratorium; Sen. Mike Jacobson plans a 2027 bill codifying it.
iw: Both major candidates now oppose new state incentives

t: Morris residents pack council meeting against Tract's 1 GW campus
b: More than 120 people attended and over 15 spoke against the Morris Technology Park, a 343-acre, 1 gigawatt site at Route 6 and Gun Club Road on land annexed and zoned in 2025. A Facebook-based opposition group plans its own meetings after the city held only virtual sessions.
iw: Organized opposition forming around an already-zoned campus

t: Columnist says Emporia data center developer disclaimed project under oath
b: McCoy reports that Gary Pinkston, promoted as the Flint Hills Digital Campus developer, told a federal bankruptcy creditors' meeting he had no interest in the project, contradicting radio remarks. The column faults the city's fast annexation and 6-1 planning vote and calls for disclosure of LLC ownership.
iw: Transparency critique ahead of Emporia's November ballot measure

t: Contractors' group argues Michigan cannot afford a blanket data center moratorium
b: In a Bridge Michigan guest commentary, the Associated Builders and Contractors chapter chief says a one-year statewide pause would likely become permanent and signal hostility to investment. He cites Public Sector Consultants and Citizens Research Council studies favoring case-by-case review with clear state standards.
iw: Construction industry pushback on SB 1018 moratorium push

t: Marshall says he backs counties that oppose data centers
b: In a KSHB voter guide, the Republican senator seeking reelection said he opposes handing land, water or power to large tech companies and supports counties resisting projects. Several Democratic primary challengers backed a temporary moratorium, local decision-making or an end to tax breaks; four did not respond.
iw: Incumbent senator aligns with local opponents

t: Edgerton council overrides planning denial of DAMAC data center
b: At a special meeting without public comment, councilmembers unanimously overturned the planning commission's denial and approved the final site plan for Dubai-based DAMAC to convert its warehouse into a data center. The commission had tabled and then denied the plan over noise and expansion questions. Neighbors announced a petition drive.
iw: Project approved over planners' objection

t: Cleveland approves three-month pause on standalone data centers
b: Council barred the city from reviewing or permitting new standalone data centers or expansions through Oct. 20, 2026, with an option to extend up to three months, while a working group studies infrastructure and zoning. Existing facilities and in-house server rooms are unaffected.
iw: Short freeze in Ohio's second-largest city

t: Whitmer unveils ratepayer plan and voluntary pledge for data centers
b: The governor proposed rules on minimum payments, contract terms, early-exit fees and collateral so households pay nothing for data center growth, plus a 10-point pledge for companies. It includes no moratorium; Sierra Club called it too weak. Oracle endorsed it.
iw: Codifies cost-shifting protections developers must absorb

t: Logan County becomes twelfth Nebraska county to pause data centers
b: Commissioners approved a 12-month moratorium on data centers that also covers wind and solar systems and cryptocurrency mining. It joined Butler, Box Butte, Custer, Dundy, Furnas, Hayes, Harlan, Johnson, Kearney, Otoe and Seward counties with temporary halts in place.
iw: Year-long county freeze; statewide count reaches twelve

t: Residents from El Dorado, Emporia and Shawnee County rally at Statehouse
b: Opponents from several communities demonstrated in Topeka against new data centers, saying projects were negotiated under nondisclosure agreements and residents learned of them after the fact. An Emporia organizer said more than 1,400 people across party lines had joined; a Democratic House candidate called the issue bipartisan.
iw: Statewide, cross-party opposition organizing

t: Asbury freezes data centers for 180 days
b: The unanimous moratorium took effect immediately so the Dubuque-area suburb can study land, infrastructure and environmental effects and write a permanent ordinance. It came a day after Dubuque County moved to hire a consultant to explore a countywide ban.
iw: Another Dubuque-area jurisdiction closes

t: Lawrence imposes 24-month data center moratorium while it writes rules
b: Commissioners voted unanimously for a moratorium of up to two years while planners draft code changes that would make data centers a special use instead of allowed by right in industrial zones. Property owners may ask for exceptions. The study covers water, energy, noise and utility costs.
iw: Two-year citywide pause plus a shift to special-use permits

t: Lincoln County rejects six-month data center moratorium a second time
b: After a three-hour meeting in North Platte, commissioners voted 3-2 against a six-month moratorium, the board's second rejection. Opponents said the county can review projects case by case; supporters wanted time to study water and energy use. Applications will continue to be considered individually.
iw: Proposed pause defeated; projects proceed case by case

t: Oshkosh tells staff to draft a 12-month data center moratorium ordinance
b: Council Member Alec Lefeber's resolution passed 6-0 with one member voting present. It directs staff to prepare a pause on buildings whose primary use is data storage, exempting ordinary server rooms, and to coordinate with neighboring governments. The ordinance returns within 60 days. No project is proposed in the city.
iw: Pause ordered up but not yet in effect

t: Wausau adopts data center zoning rules with a 200-foot residential buffer
b: The 11-0 ordinance defines data centers, requires a conditional use permit in medium and heavy industrial districts, and makes applicants report water use, energy demand, wastewater, noise and sustainability. The 200-foot setback passed 8-3. The Plan Commission decides permits. No project is pending; the council revisits the rules Sept. 22.
iw: Permit path exists but with new review and disclosure hurdles

t: Recall drive targets three Lincoln County commissioners who rejected moratorium
b: A resident filed recall petitions against commissioners Joe Hewgley, Chris Bruns and Jerry Woodruff after the board voted down a six-month data center moratorium, saying they ignored constituents. Organizers need signatures equal to 35 percent of each district's voters. Bruns said existing zoning already lets the county reject harmful projects.
iw: Political backlash against a pro-development vote

t: St. Charles County bans large data centers for six months
b: The council unanimously paused developments over 100,000 square feet or 5 MW to study effects on health, water, energy bills and quality of life, and discussed a permanent ban. Members said they may extend the pause when it expires. The city of St. Charles had prohibited data centers in May.
iw: Fast-growing suburban county closes for six months

t: Wisconsin PSC lets We Energies data center tariff appeal die
b: Commissioners declined to take up a rehearing petition from We Energies, Vantage, Cloverleaf and Oracle seeking lower collateral requirements, so the petition failed by operation of law. The April order, requiring 15-year contracts and full payment for new plants, stands.
iw: Strict credit and cost terms locked in for Wisconsin hyperscale projects

t: Neosho adopts one-year moratorium on data center construction
b: The council unanimously paused construction for up to a year, or less if research finishes sooner, to study effects on property values, residents, water and power. The vote came as Geronimo Power floated a data center park with a 2,000-acre solar farm north of Sarcoxie in neighboring Jasper County.
iw: Full one-year construction ban

t: Residents sue to overturn Sangamon County's approval of CyrusOne's campus
b: Neighbors of the 280-acre Talkington Township site challenge the board's 17-10 April conditional-use vote, saying the petition was incomplete and utility will-serve letters referred to a different, smaller project. The county asked Judge Adam Giganti to dismiss; an Oct. 9 hearing was postponed with no new date.
iw: Approved hyperscale project faces litigation risk

t: Elk River refuses zoning change for 60,000-square-foot data center
b: The council rejected an ordinance amendment that would have let Elk River Capital and Swervo Development convert an industrial building into a data center, and directed staff to draft a one-year moratorium. The related conditional-use permit was expected to be denied in August.
iw: Project blocked and a pause ordered up

t: Hermantown advances Google project with new reimbursement agreements
b: Councilors approved $200,000 more from Mortenson for planning and $20,000 from Minnesota Power so the city can run an environmental review of a transmission line to the site, after a closed session on lawsuits over the project. Dozens of residents objected to the process.
iw: City keeps processing the project amid litigation

t: Independence pauses new data centers for 180 days but exempts Nebius and Patmos
b: The unanimous resolution halts new data center and battery storage projects while zoning is updated. It does not cover the 1.2 GW Nebius campus approved in March or Patmos's pending 50 MW warehouse application; the sponsor said applying it to projects in progress would not survive a court challenge.
iw: Pause spares the two active projects

t: West Chicago pauses data center and battery storage approvals for 180 days
b: The council voted 12-0 for Ordinance 26-O-0011, halting new applications and approvals in all zoning districts while staff draft rules. A Colovore liquid-cooled facility already under construction on West Washington Street, approved by right in 2024, is unaffected. Mayor Daniel Bovey cited an explosion of inquiries.
iw: Six-month freeze in a DuPage County data center market

t: Texas Township 12-month data center moratorium takes effect
b: The Kalamazoo County township joined neighboring Portage and Oshtemo Township in pausing data center development while its planning commission studies farmland, rural zoning, infrastructure capacity, noise and light.
iw: Kalamazoo area now largely closed to new projects

t: Linn County stops EU-3 data center rezonings through January 2028
b: The board, with Sami Scheetz opposed, will not accept applications to rezone unincorporated land to the EU-3 Large-Scale Data Center District until 11:59 p.m. Jan. 1, 2028, unless it acts sooner, saying its February ordinance predated new information on cumulative water, grid, road and emergency impacts. Cities are not covered.
iw: Rezoning freeze next to the Cedar Rapids campuses

t: Three in four Wisconsin voters say data center costs outweigh benefits
b: The July survey of 838 registered voters found 76% saying costs outweigh benefits, up from 55% in October 2025. Majorities of Republicans (67%), independents (71%) and Democrats (88%) agreed, though only 5% called data centers their top issue.
iw: Bipartisan opposition hardening in a key state

t: Kehoe refuses special session, says SB 4 already protects ratepayers
b: The governor said on 93.9 The Eagle he will not call lawmakers back, arguing the 2025 law already makes large users pay for their power and that siting is a local decision. The House scheduled a September hearing on transparency and public-comment rules instead.
iw: No new statewide restrictions before 2027 session

t: PSC approves power project for Applied Digital's Polaris Forge 2 near Harwood
b: Regulators approved a roughly $110 million power project serving Applied Digital's second Polaris Forge campus in Cass County, described as nearing completion. The company's Ellendale campus energized another 75 MW the same month and pre-leased a 430 MW third campus to a hyperscale customer in May.
iw: State approval keeps a hyperscale buildout on schedule

t: Braun order directs state to seek reopening or retaining coal plants
b: An executive order directs the Secretary of Energy and Natural Resources to look for opportunities to reopen retired coal plants or keep units from retiring, which Sierra Club says is aimed at powering proposed AI data centers. The order itself does not name data centers.
iw: State pushes supply-side support for large loads

t: Seward County pauses data center permits and construction for a year
b: Commissioners unanimously adopted a 12-month pause on all data center construction, permits and special-use conditions, with two members absent. The pause stays in effect unless the planning board and commissioners adopt data center regulations before it ends.
iw: Twelve-month county-wide freeze

t: Springfield adopts 120-day administrative delay on data center development
b: The council approved a pause so staff can review existing regulations, analyze land use compatibility, electric, water, wastewater, noise and air impacts, and build a public-interest evaluation framework with open houses. Recommendations go to the Planning and Zoning Commission and council. No specific project was named.
iw: Third-largest city pauses while writing rules

t: Kansas Reflector columnist urges moratorium after Emporia hearing draws 400
b: McCoy describes a six-hour Emporia planning hearing on the 1,000-acre Flint Hills Digital Campus where speakers ran about five to one against, notes the developer's recent Chapter 11 filing, and argues local governments lack the expertise to set safety rules, so a pause is needed until national standards exist.
iw: Statewide column backing a pause amid Emporia fight

t: Inver Grove Heights passes one-year moratorium despite $150 million lawsuit threat
b: The council voted 3-2 at an early-morning meeting to pause data center construction while studying grid and environmental impacts. Florida-based QLevr, proposing a 5 MW, 55,000-square-foot facility on Carmen Avenue, had warned of damages over $150 million. Residents also petitioned for an environmental review.
iw: Pause adopted over explicit litigation threat

t: Minneapolis adopts six-month pause on large data centers
b: The ordinance blocks new, re-established or expanded data centers and related zoning and building permits while planning staff study impacts; downtown projects under 350,000 square feet are exempt. The council must revisit it by Nov. 21. An earlier resolution passed 8-5 in May.
iw: Largest city in the state halts big projects

t: Woodbury County halts data center applications for 12 months
b: The 5-0 resolution bars accepting or processing data center projects in unincorporated areas while supervisors research the issue and hear from the public. It does not cover existing or approved facilities or the 900 acres Salix annexed for a possible site.
iw: Unincorporated land off limits for a year

t: Cedar Rapids clears Google occupancy step as member floats moratorium
b: The council approved an indemnification agreement letting Google obtain a temporary occupancy permit for its first building near the airport, with David Maier opposed. Ashley Vanorny said the city should consider pausing further projects until the two under construction prove their water and energy claims.
iw: Project advances, but pause talk begins

t: Carbondale adopts a one-year hold on data center development
b: The council voted 4-1 for a resolution pausing new data centers while staff study impacts and draft zoning rules; council member Nancy Maxwell wanted more study and state action first. Mayor Caroline Harvey called it proactive, since no developer had approached the city. Residents cited water, power and noise.
iw: Pre-emptive twelve-month pause in southern Illinois

t: Janesville lets Viridian's GM-site data center agreement lapse, orders guardrails
b: The council unanimously refused a 60-day extension of its letter of intent with Viridian Acquisitions for a hyperscale project at the former GM/JATCO plant and directed staff to draft a data center ordinance. An amendment to halt all developer talks until rules exist failed 4-3. Nearly every speaker opposed renewal.
iw: Hyperscale talks at the city's biggest site are over

t: Jackson County halts data center and battery storage applications for 180 days
b: Legislators voted 8-0 to stop processing land use applications for data centers and battery energy storage systems while the county writes safety standards, setbacks from homes and stronger public notice rules. County Executive Phil LeVota said he has supported a pause; projects already underway are not expected to be affected.
iw: Kansas City's home county freezes new applications

t: FERC orders MISO and SPP to justify or rewrite large-load rules
b: Show cause orders to all six grid operators, including MISO and SPP, say their tariffs may be unjust for failing to set large-load study rules, cost-recovery agreements, co-location terms and flexible service. Responses were due Aug. 17, with up to 90 days of abeyance to draft stakeholder reforms.
iw: Pushes faster, clearer interconnection paths but with cost-assignment strings

t: Kehoe calls data center concerns misinformation at Rolla AI forum
b: Speaking to about 200 people at Missouri S&T, the governor praised data centers' economic benefits, suggested foreign adversaries may be fueling opposition and took no questions. Small protests outside focused on water use and ticket access. Rep. Tricia Byrnes used the event to call for a statewide hyperscale moratorium.
iw: Governor signals no appetite for state limits

t: Logan County's 12-month data center moratorium ruled invalid by its own state's attorney
b: State's Attorney Bradley Hauge said the May 19 pause skipped a required zoning board advisory vote and public hearings, after Hut 8 threatened to sue. He directed staff to accept Hut 8's applications for a 500 MW campus near Latham. The board also failed 5-6 to adopt zoning rules.
iw: Pause that froze a $5 billion project is void

t: IURC approves NIPSCO's Amazon special contract and large-load settlement
b: The commission approved a settlement, Amazon's special contract and a related power purchase agreement for data center load in northern Indiana, and separately approved NIPSCO's gas and battery resources. NiSource says data center customers fund the generation and transmission serving them and existing customers get bill credits as load ramps.
iw: Clears Amazon's northern Indiana supply deal with cost protections

t: Superior passes a one-year data center moratorium with no project pending
b: Councilor Garner Moffat proposed the precautionary pause, backed by Mayor Jim Paine, while the city rewrites its planning and zoning code; data centers are not currently a permitted use. Paine said Minnesota Power had floated a Superior site for what became Google's Hermantown proposal and the city declined.
iw: Twin Ports city closed to data centers for a year

t: Webster County pauses data centers, solar, wind and batteries for six months
b: The order covers unincorporated areas while the county, which has no planning and zoning, studies health, emergency response, stormwater, noise, and water and power use and decides what legal tools it has. The county says it does not intend to halt the data center under construction on Rifle Range Road.
iw: Blanket pause on energy-intensive uses

t: Bourbonnais becomes first Kankakee County town to pause data centers
b: Trustees voted 4-0 for a moratorium inside village limits that expires Jan. 31, 2027. More than 100 residents attended amid rumors of a project; officials said none was proposed and the pause gives the village time to set rules.
iw: Village-wide pause through January 2027

t: Developer sues Eagan over the state's first data center moratorium
b: Eagan Capital's complaint argues the city lacks authority to suspend data centers and that only the PUC regulates electricity demand. Eagan had denied its interim use permit in May after unpermitted chiller units were found. The one-year pause began in February.
iw: Court test of city moratorium power, outcome open

t: Adams County imposes two-year data center moratorium
b: Resolution 2026-25, adopted 4-0, bars the county from accepting or approving any land-use permits for data centers, including substations and backup power, and prohibits related grading or construction for 24 months unless the board acts sooner. Individual applications may still be submitted for consideration.
iw: Longest pause in Iowa so far at 24 months

t: Council Bluffs unanimously rejects mayor's one-year data center pause
b: Mayor Jill Shudak sought a moratorium to replace 2007-era zoning rules and address water and sewer limits. Members said a pause would signal the city is closed for business and preferred new rules and a wastewater plan handled case by case.
iw: Major Google host city stays open

t: Boone County halts data center applications in unincorporated areas for a year
b: Commissioners unanimously adopted a moratorium, effective June 16 and running through June 15, 2027, on filing, processing or approving applications for new data centers outside city and town limits. The Area Plan Commission recommended it in May as the county updates its comprehensive plan; officials may study an outright ban.
iw: Pause in the county hosting LEAP and Meta's Lebanon campus

t: Edgerton and Gardner reject six-month data center moratoriums
b: Edgerton's council voted 3-2 against a six-month halt on applications for facilities whose primary use is a data center, without discussion. Gardner's council had turned down a similar proposal on June 1. Residents in southern Johnson County had pushed both cities to pause.
iw: Two proposed pauses defeated in a targeted growth corridor

t: Nessel seeks tougher terms in DTE's 1 GW Google contract
b: In contested-case testimony on DTE's 20-year contracts for Google's Van Buren Township campus, the attorney general asked regulators to raise minimum monthly charges from 80% to at least 90% of demand, increase exit fees and add cost-tracking so residents do not subsidize transmission or supply costs.
iw: Pressure for stricter take-or-pay and exit terms on hyperscale deals

t: Alliant-commissioned study says data centers need not raise Iowa, Wisconsin rates
b: Brattle's white paper argues Alliant's Iowa and Wisconsin utilities are insulated from cost shifting because large-load contracts cover at least incremental costs, and that past rate growth stayed near inflation. Critics later cited it as industry spin in the peaker-plant fight.
iw: Industry evidence against cost-shift claims in two states

t: McLean County adopts data center zoning rules on water, power and decommissioning
b: Adopted without debate on the consent agenda, the rules require impact assessments for roads and services, disclosure of water sources and groundwater effects, wastewater and electricity monitoring plans, fire district training or equipment and a funded decommissioning plan. Officials called them stricter than neighboring counties'; there is no moratorium.
iw: New disclosure and planning burdens, but no pause

t: Ohio lawmakers leave for recess without votes to pass data center bill
b: Substitute HB 646, which would halve the sales tax exemption for new projects, require closed-loop cooling, address NDAs and create a data center rate class, lacked votes in both chambers before summer recess. Speaker Huffman said a veto override on incentives was unlikely; the House planned to return June 24.
iw: Statewide restrictions stall for now

t: Montgomery County grants Google 25-year Chapter 100 abatement for $15 billion campus
b: Commissioners unanimously approved up to $100 billion in industrial revenue bonds and a 70% personal property tax abatement from 2028 to 2052 for Project Spade near New Florence. Google pays full real estate taxes and 30% PILOTs; fire and ambulance districts are kept whole. Residents cite water use and NDAs.
iw: Second hyperscale incentive package in one rural county

t: Pritzker orders DCEO to stop processing data center incentive agreements
b: Directive pauses new agreements under the 2019 data center tax exemption program from July 1 with no end date, pending a legislative framework on energy, water and community agreements. Labor groups called it shortsighted; environmental groups backed it. Twenty-seven data centers got $983 million in breaks from 2020 to 2024.
iw: State sales tax exemption closed to new projects indefinitely

t: FERC approves SPP conditional service letting data centers connect before upgrades
b: The Conditional High Impact Large Load Service lets SPP, which covers Kansas, Nebraska, the Dakotas and parts of Missouri and Iowa, serve data centers on curtailable terms for up to seven years while firm service and generation are built. It took effect July 1.
iw: Years-faster grid access across the SPP footprint

t: Dane County bars hyperscale data center zoning permits for 18 months
b: Supervisors unanimously blocked applications and permits for facilities with 5,000-plus servers and 10,000-plus square feet in the 26 towns under county zoning, through December 2027. Modeled on Manitowoc County, it targets permitting to sidestep the state ban on development moratoriums. Cities and villages are not covered.
iw: Hyperscale projects shut out of rural Dane County into late 2027

t: Senate bills would impose a one-year statewide data center moratorium
b: SBs 1018–1020 would pause new data center projects for a year with $1,000-a-day fines for operating in violation; projects under construction could finish but not open. The Republican's package was referred to the Senate Government Operations Committee.
iw: Statewide pause bill, though leadership prefers regulation

t: Effingham freezes data center and crypto mine permits for a year
b: The 5-0 vote stops applications, permitting and approvals for data centers and cryptocurrency mines within city limits and the 1.5-mile extraterritorial zone for 12 months so the city can research the industry.
iw: Twelve-month permit freeze at an interstate crossroads city

t: Brown County committee declines to take up a countywide data center moratorium
b: The planning committee said a county pause would have no effect because every municipality in Brown County has its own zoning. Instead, three supervisors will informally survey local governments. Supervisor Christopher Welch had sought a pause until state rules exist.
iw: Proposed pause in the Green Bay area goes nowhere

t: Oracle sues Wisconsin regulators over data center collateral rules
b: Oracle asked Ozaukee County Circuit Court to set aside the credit-rating and collateral conditions the Public Service Commission attached to We Energies' very large customer tariff, saying they could require more than $7 billion in letters of credit for the Port Washington campus it shares with OpenAI and Vantage.
iw: Court test of how much security states can demand from developers

t: Sixteen Missouri House Republicans ask Kehoe for data center special session
b: The letter says development is moving too fast to wait for January, citing strain on water, power, roads and quality of life. A Missouri Rural Crisis Center survey of Montgomery County voters found nearly 85% of 1,461 respondents opposed the New Florence project.
iw: GOP backlash spreading through Missouri primaries

t: Butler County imposes six-month data center pause in six townships
b: Commissioners adopted a six-month moratorium covering six of the county's 13 townships, those under county zoning, as Trenton and other Butler County cities drew Amazon projects. Fayette County later followed with a pause for its unincorporated townships.
s: News From The States (Ohio Capital Journal)
iw: Freeze across unincorporated Butler County

t: Jerome Township's early moratorium expires; projects proceed under new rules
b: The Union County township's nine-month pause, one of Ohio's first, lapsed in June. Data centers are now in development there under land-use restrictions trustees adopted in March 2026, after residents complained about noise from existing facilities.
s: News From The States (Ohio Capital Journal)
iw: Development resumes with conditions in a Columbus-area hotspot

t: Armstrong warns developers not to raise rates, cautions locals against NDAs
b: The governor said North Dakota's approach should rest on infrastructure capacity, local decision-making and openness. He told developers to work with local leaders, warned against any consumer rate increases, discouraged nondisclosure agreements with local officials, and said regulation should track resource use rather than industry type. He expects 2027 legislation.
iw: No new rules, but ratepayer and transparency expectations set

t: DeWine halts review of new data center tax exemption requests
b: The governor directed the Ohio Tax Credit Authority to stop taking new data center sales tax exemption applications while a joint legislative committee studies the industry's growth. The pause has no end date and does not restrict construction; existing exemptions are untouched.
iw: New projects lose access to the state's main incentive for now

t: Dubuque County adopts 12-month data center moratorium on 2-1 vote
b: Supervisors stretched a proposed 120-day pause to a year for unincorporated areas while staff draft zoning rules, with town halls planned. The dissenter wanted more legal review. A developer had asked the city of Dubuque about water and sewer connections.
iw: Year-long county pause near an active proposal

t: Bloomington unanimously pauses data centers above 5 MW for six months
b: The moratorium covers facilities designed for more than 5 megawatts and requires at least two public hearings before it ends; the council can extend it. Council member Abby Scott said the goal is regulations like Aurora's and McLean County's. Normal adopted its own pause earlier in May.
iw: Six-month freeze on projects over 5 MW

t: Logan County pauses data centers for a year, stalling Hut 8's $5 billion plan
b: The board voted 6-4 after amending a proposed 90-day pause to 12 months. The developer had promised roughly $65 million a year in property taxes; opponents wanted time to understand the project.
iw: Multi-billion-dollar project frozen for twelve months

t: Wright County bars data center applications in its townships for a year
b: Ordinance 26-2, adopted unanimously after 14 residents spoke in support, pauses applications across the county's 18 townships while it writes setbacks and other land-use rules. The chair said the goal is conditions, not prohibition. Monticello's city ordinance is unaffected.
iw: Countywide application freeze for up to a year

t: Otoe County suspends data center permits for up to a year
b: Commissioners voted to stop issuing data center permits for up to twelve months while the county studies impacts and updates its regulations. Tenaska has optioned land in Otoe and Gage counties. Madison County separately added a special-permit requirement earlier in May.
iw: Year-long permit freeze in a county with an optioned site

t: Minnesota session ends with no new data center restrictions
b: A two-year hyperscale moratorium from Sen. Jen McEwen, a ban on local officials signing NDAs and separate water-permit rules all stalled before adjournment after building trades and industry groups pushed back. The 2025 ratepayer law remains the state's main rule.
iw: Statewide pause, NDA ban and water bills all died

t: Riley County data center moratorium runs through mid-November
b: The county's roughly six-month moratorium began May 18 and is set to end Nov. 12. The planning director says the county wants regulations or limits in place before it expires and has not ruled out an extension.
iw: Six-month county pause with a possible extension

t: Elwood-area residents sue to void Joliet's approval of the $20 billion campus
b: Filed against Joliet and the Hillwood-affiliated developers, the suit says the plan commission notice hid that the project was a data center, the March 19 vote broke the Open Meetings Act, the rezoning is unconstitutional and the campus would draw 150,000 gallons daily from an aquifer.
iw: Approved campus faces a challenge to its approvals

t: PUC approves Xcel's very large customer tariff with stiffer exit terms
b: Regulators adopted Xcel's framework for new loads of 100 MW or more (20 MW if system-intensive) in docket 25-289: a separate rate class, 15-year default contracts, 24-month exit notice, minimum bills and exit fees at 80% of contracted capacity, and direct payment for grid upgrades.
iw: Long contracts and 80% exit fees raise commitment costs

t: PSC approves Meta's Beaver Dam power deal with conditions, orders a standard tariff
b: Alliant's 220 MW contract with a Meta affiliate was approved with termination charges through the 10-year term, a Meta backstop, cost studies, reporting and a Focus on Energy contribution. Alliant must file a public large-load tariff for future customers of 100 MW or more. The chair criticized the deal's secrecy.
iw: Project proceeds, but future deals move to a public tariff

t: House bill would permanently end Ohio's data center sales tax exemption
b: HB 975, introduced the day DeWine paused new exemption reviews, would repeal the exemption effective Oct. 1, 2026. A Senate companion, SB 374, would end it a year later. The bill sits in committee with no hearing scheduled.
iw: Signals pressure to end the state's core incentive

t: Judge halts construction at Google's Pine Island site pending environmental suit
b: A temporary restraining order bars work on Project Skyway while the Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy's case against the city and Ryan Companies proceeds; the next hearing is Nov. 16. State air, stormwater and PUC transmission reviews are still pending for the roughly 500-acre campus.
iw: Court order freezes a flagship hyperscale project

t: Iowa data center reporting and tariff bill dies without a floor vote
b: HF 2690 cleared House Commerce 23-0 in February and would have required quarterly water and energy reports, a separate utility customer class and a halt to new construction until tariffs were filed, but never reached the floor before adjournment in early May.
iw: Disclosure and tariff mandates failed

t: Cap Times urges Dane County to adopt 18-month data center moratorium
b: The Madison paper called moratoriums reasonable and necessary, backing the county pause for 26 zoned towns so an advisory committee can study energy, water and land impacts. The board adopted the moratorium in June, joining Madison, Westport and Manitowoc County.
iw: Major regional paper endorsing pauses

t: Manitowoc County adopts an 18-month data center moratorium, longer than proposed
b: Supervisors unanimously approved the pause after lengthening it from the original 12 months, saying the county needs time to research and write zoning rules for any data center applicant. Three lakeshore towns had already enacted their own pauses. The approach was later copied by Dane County.
iw: County-zoned land closed to data centers into late 2027

t: PSC rewrites We Energies' data center tariff: 15-year terms, full cost recovery
b: Regulators approved the very-large-customer tariff with major changes: minimum contracts go to 15 years, the threshold drops from 500 MW to 100 MW, customers pay 100 percent of their costs, and a capacity-only option is removed. The utility must address transmission cost shifting and report on agreements.
iw: Longer commitments and full cost responsibility for large loads

t: Westport caps new data centers at 10,000 square feet for a year
b: The Dane County town's board voted 4-1 for a one-year moratorium limiting any new data center to 10,000 square feet, modeled on Madison's and Dane County's measures. Supervisors cited farmland loss and the fight over QTS's rejected 1,500-acre annexation bid in nearby DeForest. One member opposed any size limit.
iw: Hyperscale development effectively barred in a Madison suburb

t: Cincinnati extends interim data center review through end of 2026
b: Council extended an Interim Development Control Overlay that requires planning commission review of any proposed data center, ending automatic approval under existing zoning, while staff study more than 22,000 downtown and industrial parcels and draft permanent rules.
iw: Discretionary review replaces by-right approval

t: ICC lets ComEd scale deposits for large loads and opens a data center inquiry
b: Projects asking for 50 to 200 MW post $1 million, rising $500,000 per additional 100 MW, replacing a flat deposit. The commission ordered staff to open a broader ratepayer-protection proceeding by April 23, to finish within about eight months. ComEd has 75-plus large-load requests totaling 28,000 MW.
iw: Higher upfront security plus a pending tariff investigation

t: Joliet approves annexation for a 795-acre, 1.8 GW data center campus
b: The council voted 8-1 for HW Technology Park Development's $20 billion Joliet Technology Center next to Chicagoland Speedway after hours of mostly opposed testimony on health and bills. The developer pledged $100 million for city services, projected $2 billion in taxes and said it needs no water for cooling.
iw: Largest data center approval in Illinois to date

t: Saline County adopts three-year pause on data centers, nuclear and hydrogen plants
b: Commissioners voted 4-0 to halt construction of data centers, nuclear power and hydrogen energy facilities in unincorporated areas for three years, a period they can shorten or extend. The stated goal is time to write regulations; some members also wanted voters to weigh in at the next election.
iw: Multi-year county-wide pause on new projects

t: Mount Pleasant unanimously approves 15 more Microsoft data centers on two campuses
b: The board signed off on nine buildings near Durand Avenue and six plus offices along International Drive, nearly 9 million square feet on former Foxconn land with taxable value that could top $13 billion. Microsoft can now file building permits. Residents raised scale and energy concerns; trades backed the jobs.
iw: Largest single local approval in the state clears the way to permits

t: Madison bars zoning approvals for principal-use data centers over 10,000 square feet
b: The one-year moratorium stops zoning approvals, building permits and occupancy certificates for new stand-alone data centers above 10,000 square feet of floor area. Server rooms serving another use on the same lot are exempt. The city must amend its zoning code by Jan. 24, 2027, when the pause ends.
iw: Year-long freeze on new data centers in the state capital

t: KCC approves Evergy large-load tariff with minimum bills and collateral
b: Regulators unanimously adopted a settlement creating Evergy's large load power service for customers at or above 75 MW. Contracts run at least 12 years after an optional ramp-up, with an 80 percent minimum monthly bill, two years of collateral, 36 months' exit notice and exit fees.
iw: Long contracts, minimum bills and collateral raise the cost of entry

t: HB 2515's comprehensive data center rules die in the Senate
b: Passed the House 51–41 but got no Senate vote. It would have required utility tariffs for facilities over 20 MW, annual energy and water reports, separate cost treatment and rising clean-power requirements.
iw: Cost and clean-power mandates avoided for now

t: SB 5982 holds data centers to Washington's clean-energy law
b: Signed March 24, effective June 11. Brings port districts and large customers that self-generate or buy power outside regulated utilities under the Clean Energy Transformation Act's deadlines and reporting, closing a route for fossil-powered sites.
iw: Closes off fossil-powered workarounds

t: Washington narrows its data center sales tax break
b: ESSB 6231 ends the exemption for replacement server equipment and refurbishments while keeping it for new construction and original equipment. An earlier version would have repealed far more.
iw: Higher costs for existing sites

t: Seattle adopts a one-year moratorium on large data centers
b: The council voted 9–0 to freeze new data centers above 20 MVA while it studies impacts, extendable six months. Five large proposals had surfaced in April; applications filed earlier remain vested.
iw: Pause in a major West Coast city

t: Spokane passes a one-year emergency data center moratorium, 6–1
b: Halts building permit applications for new data centers. It came weeks after Avista disclosed interest from a 500 MW project, and was amended to cover data centers inside mixed-use sites.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Spokane County extends its data center permit pause to June 2027
b: Commissioners unanimously extended the halt on accepting and processing data center permits until June 1, 2027, or until rules are adopted. Critics said the work plan still leaves loopholes.
iw: Longer county pause

t: Rallies at 19 Washington sites demand a statewide data center moratorium
b: Hundreds turned out in Seattle, Spokane, Olympia, Walla Walla and elsewhere. A moratorium bill is expected in 2027, though the governor's workgroup favors rules over a pause.
iw: Builds pressure for a 2027 pause bill

t: Klickitat County resists a pause as six hyperscale proposals seek 5.6 GW
b: Developers have requested up to 5,655 MW from Bonneville and the county PUD. Commissioners declined a moratorium and are drafting rules for 20 MW-plus sites; Skamania, Benton, Yakima and Hood River counties all paused.
iw: No pause yet, rules coming

t: Port of Walla Walla finalizes a $36 million land sale to Amazon
b: Commissioners unanimously approved selling about 554 acres at Wallula Gap for a planned 16-building, roughly $4.8 billion campus. An NDA had kept Amazon's identity secret since 2023; the county is reviewing its site plan.
iw: Land secured for a large campus

t: Reno becomes Nevada's first city to pause data center permits
b: Voted 6–1 for a pending moratorium on new conditional use permits, exempting four projects already in the pipeline. On June 1 it voted 6–1 again to extend the pause through Aug. 31, 2027, or until new rules pass.
iw: Pause in a major market

t: Henderson rejects a 180-day data center moratorium
b: The council chose individually negotiated development agreements instead, with standards on water, power, noise and distance from homes. The city attorney said code changes would last longer than a pause; Henderson has no pending applications.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Nye County bans data centers in the Pahrump groundwater basin
b: Nevada's first outright local ban covers the over-appropriated Basin 162, where Gigawatt Development Partners planned the Manse Technology Campus. It followed a June countywide moratorium; rules for the rest of the county came later.
iw: Permanent ban in a large basin

t: Nevada lawmakers draft a bill to end data center tax breaks and pause construction
b: The Joint Interim Standing Committee on Revenue voted to draft Sen. Dina Neal's bill for the 2027 session. Nevada has granted about $461 million in expected data center tax breaks over 11 years.
iw: Possible end to incentives

t: Lombardo's order makes tax-break seekers pay school taxes and cover power costs
b: Executive Order 2026-005 bars abatement applications unless developers pay the Local School Support Tax in full and sign a binding commitment on water, ratepayer costs and grid emergencies. Terms are due Nov. 6.
iw: Smaller incentives, more conditions

t: Ford pledges to pause data center tax breaks and let communities say no
b: The Democratic nominee called Lombardo's order a last-ditch move and backs a statewide evaporative-cooling ban. Lombardo's camp notes Ford co-sponsored the 2015 abatement law.
iw: Challenger favors tighter limits

t: Hill County rescinds Texas's first county moratorium after a $100 million suit
b: The 3–2 May pause covered unincorporated areas facing eight proposals. RCM Hill, developer of Project Aquila, sued in federal court, and the county swapped the pause for a developer disclosure checklist.
iw: Shows the legal limits on county pauses

t: Somervell County formally opposes new data centers until lawmakers act
b: Unanimous resolution after an earlier moratorium proposal failed. It has no binding effect.
iw: Symbolic

t: Hood County rejects a data center moratorium, 3–2
b: A state senator had warned the county off. Van Zandt County separately paused green energy projects the same month.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Hays County defers abatements and development deals for data centers
b: After tabling a moratorium twice over legal doubts, the county adopted a 180-day review period through year-end covering the approvals it controls: abatements, development agreements and variances.
iw: Slower county incentives

t: Austin County pauses AI data centers and battery storage projects
b: Unanimous countywide moratorium west of Houston, framed as time to set standards rather than a ban. CleanSpark had urged the county not to delay its planned 285 MW campus near Sealy.
iw: County pause

t: Athens bans data centers within city limits, 3–2
b: Passed after a long fight with residents who opposed a proposed build.
iw: City ban

t: Lewisville bars data centers from residential areas and requires special permits
b: New applications get two public hearings. North Richland Hills adopted a similar permit rule in July.
iw: More review, not a ban

t: Fort Worth starts the process for a 90-day data center moratorium
b: Council members voted in mid-August to initiate the pause; Denton began a similar process the same month.
iw: Possible pause in a major city

t: Coachella permanently bans data centers
b: The Coachella Valley's first permanent ban took effect Sept. 25, after backlash over a canceled campus deal with a Stronghold Power Systems subsidiary. Accessory server rooms are exempt.
iw: Permanent city ban

t: Fresno begins drafting a 10-year citywide data center ban
b: The 7–0 vote directs staff to draft the ban, which would become permanent after 10 years unless a later council changes it. Mayor Jerry Dyer co-sponsored it.
iw: Possible long ban in a large city

t: Calexico bans data centers through its zoning code
b: The 3–0 amendment makes data centers a prohibited use. In July the council had passed on a temporary moratorium in favor of a permanent ban.
iw: City ban

t: Tulare County extends its data center moratorium by 10 months
b: The 5–0 vote extends an Aug. 18 pause to August 2027 while staff draft permanent rules. The same day, supervisors voted 3–2 to formally oppose data centers in the county.
iw: Long county pause

t: Oakland adopts a 45-day emergency data center moratorium
b: Unanimous. The pause followed a developer's plan to turn part of a downtown office building into a data center. San Francisco supervisors approved their own 45-day pause the same week.
iw: Short pause in a large city

t: Imperial County reinstates its moratorium after a court loss
b: Supervisors voted 5–0 to repeal the struck ordinances and adopt a new 45-day pause with added findings, citing a Sept. 10 ruling that requires full environmental review of the Imperial Data Center project. Two supervisors want a public vote.
iw: Pause restored, a project halted

t: HB 5594–5596 would halt Michigan data center permits until April 2027
b: The bipartisan Data Center Regulation Act would bar state and local permits and new operations. It sits in committee, and Gov. Whitmer's office says she would veto any moratorium.
iw: Statewide pause, unlikely to become law

t: Wixom swaps its moratorium for strict data center zoning
b: Rules adopted Aug. 26 set a 1,500-foot setback, required sound studies and water-use standards, ending the six-month pause early by Sept. 6. Developer Wixom Industrial One is suing over the pause in federal court.
iw: Tough siting rules

t: Zeeland Township pauses data centers and energy facilities for a year
b: Unanimous. It repealed and replaced a March data center pause, adding energy facilities, while the township updates its master plan and challenges a state solar-siting law in court.
iw: One-year pause

t: Pere Marquette Township adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: The township board took up a one-year pause in July with no proposal pending, and the planning commission backed a zoning version in August so it could take effect by September.
iw: Local pauses

t: Hawkins County permanently bans data centers and crypto mines
b: Passed 10–2. Crypto company ExoticRidge sued in March 2026, backed by the Beacon Center; the case is a test of local bans in Tennessee.
iw: Permanent county ban

t: Washington County, Tennessee, pauses data centers through June 2027
b: Passed 13–2 and also covers crypto mining.
iw: County pause

t: Bristol, Johnson City and neighbors pause or restrict data centers
b: Bristol adopted a two-year moratorium and Johnson City extended its pause to December. Jonesborough requires 1,500-foot residential buffers, and Kingsport limits data centers to heavy industrial zones.
iw: Regional pauses and limits

t: Morristown adopts its first data center zoning rules, 6–1
b: Data centers are limited to heavy industrial zones with review, 500 feet from homes, schools and government buildings, with all equipment indoors. The council chose rules over a moratorium; Hamblen County has a separate one-year pause.
iw: Rules rather than a pause

t: More than 100 New Jersey towns have now banned data centers
b: Colts Neck and Cranbury adopted bans in mid-October, pushing advocates' count past 100; Pemberton went first in February. Gov. Sherrill has resisted a statewide moratorium.
iw: Most of the state's towns closing off

t: Developer sues Andover Township over its reversal to a data center ban
b: The township had zoned a 100-acre former airport for data centers in 2025, then switched to a ban days after a rowdy meeting. Montgomery, Monroe and Millville also face developer suits.
iw: Tests how far town bans can go

t: New Jersey Senate passes a bill voiding data center NDAs, 38–0
b: S4304 would bar data center applicants from agreements with approving authorities, municipal agencies or land sellers that conceal plans or block public review. It cleared the Community and Urban Affairs Committee 4–1 on Oct. 1; the Assembly version, A2774, is still in committee.
iw: More disclosure

t: Washington County, Florida, adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: Unanimous; it halts applications in unincorporated areas. Equipment incidental to a property's main use that fills no more than 5% of its floor area is exempt.
iw: County pause

t: Walton County bans data centers; DeSoto, Pensacola and Flagler adopt pauses
b: Walton banned data centers and large-load centers outright June 9, 5–0. DeSoto adopted a moratorium in early July, Pensacola gave first approval July 16 to a one-year pause on 50 MW-plus projects, and Flagler adopted a one-year pause Aug. 3.
iw: Spreading pauses

t: Town of Tonawanda pauses data centers of 20 MW or more for a year
b: Unanimous vote. It mirrors the governor's statewide pause at a lower threshold and covers the stalled 300 MW proposal at the former Tonawanda Coke site, which never filed a complete application.
iw: Town pause

t: Buffalo approves a two-year data center pause, pending a local law
b: The council's resolution covers data centers of 20 MW or more and crypto mining, amended to create a nine-member task force to draft rules. City lawyers say a local law is needed to make it binding, and Mayor Ryan is reviewing it.
iw: Possible two-year city pause

t: Potsdam holds a hearing on a 12-month large data center moratorium
b: Proposed two days after nearby Massena voted 3–2 against a pause, clearing the way for a roughly 400 MW project. It would cover data centers of 20 MW or 50,000 sq ft and crypto mines of 5 MW.
iw: Possible town pause

t: Old Town adopts a six-month data center moratorium in industrial zones
b: Unanimous and retroactive to Sept. 8; data centers are already barred in other zones. Councilors want any permanent zoning ban put to a referendum, possibly in June 2027.
iw: City pause

t: Hillsboro approves 17 stacked tax breaks just before its moratorium
b: Operators applied for successive five-year incentives that could run for decades, a use state officials said they had never seen. Public anger turned the city against its longtime industry.
iw: Long-running incentives locked in

t: Kotek blocks state land sale for a $5 billion Salem data center
b: Stopped the sale of a 32-acre state parcel at Salem's Mill Creek Corporate Center after residents objected to a California developer's plan.
iw: Project site lost

t: Hillsboro cuts land open to standalone data centers from 6,600 to 608 acres
b: Caps include already-approved sites, leaving about 30 acres for new ones. Adds public hearings, limits accessory data centers and a temporary 1,000-foot school buffer. Forest Grove adopted a 120-day pause Oct. 12.
iw: Little room left in a top Oregon hub

t: Yakima County adopts a six-month data center moratorium
b: Unanimous; no land use or building permits for data centers in unincorporated areas while the county studies water, power, health and farm impacts. No applications had been filed.
iw: Preemptive county pause

t: Pierce County bars new data centers over 10 MW for a year
b: An emergency ordinance covers new and expanded facilities in unincorporated areas around Tacoma, running to August 2027 unless lifted.
iw: County pause near a major metro

t: Grant PUD proposes separate, higher rate classes for data centers in 2027
b: Data centers used about 37% of Grant County's electricity in 2025. New High Density Compute classes would pay 4.5 to 4.8 cents per kWh under a growth-pays-for-growth approach; budget hearings are Oct. 27.
iw: Higher power costs in the Quincy hub

t: Washington regulators open a review of large-load interconnection and tariffs
b: Docket UE-260162 is a commission-led workshop series on how big loads connect and pay. Public utilities argue a statewide model would undercut local commissions.
iw: Rules still being shaped

t: Oregon regulators raise PGE's data center rates 29.7% under the POWER Act
b: A May 7 order created a separate class for loads over 20 MW with long contracts, exit fees and clean-energy conditions. Residential rates fell 1.3%. A Pacific Power decision is due later this year.
iw: Much higher power costs

t: Oregon Democrats plan a three-year moratorium bill for 2027
b: Sens. Jeff Golden and Courtney Neron Misslin and Reps. Lesly Muñoz and Farrah Chaichi will propose it, citing energy and water demand, farmland loss and tax breaks.
iw: Possible long statewide pause

t: Kotek's data center advisers publish findings but no recommendations yet
b: The preliminary report found about 9,000 acres proposed for data centers and questioned generous tax breaks; roughly 90% of comments opposed more data centers. Final recommendations come after the election.
iw: Points toward tighter oversight

t: Woodburn adopts a 120-day data center moratorium
b: Unanimous, with no pending applications. Verrus had explored a site in the city but says it has no near-term plans there.
iw: City pause

t: Salem's moratorium blocks Verrus's $5.1 billion Mill Creek campus until January
b: The 120-day pause runs through Jan. 19 and can be extended. Verrus had applied for a 600,000 sq ft first phase days before the city began the process; residents cited the Santiam River water supply.
iw: Large project on hold

t: Umatilla declares an emergency over Kotek's data center permit pause
b: Eastern Oregon officials say the pause costs them fees and infrastructure money. Hermiston says Amazon canceled several planned campuses, and a Morrow County commissioner called it executive overreach.
iw: Local pushback against the state pause

t: Clackamas County adopts a 120-day data center moratorium
b: Unanimous, after two public hearings, covering unincorporated areas while staff draft rules.
iw: County pause near Portland

t: Los Angeles County pauses hyperscale data centers in unincorporated areas
b: The planning director froze approvals pending a permanent ban sought by Supervisor Hilda Solis. The board postponed its Oct. 6 vote on that ban after heavy public comment.
iw: Pause in the largest county

t: San Francisco adopts a 45-day citywide data center moratorium, 11–0
b: An urgency ordinance covering new data centers, expansions and power upgrades while the city revisits 20-year-old rules.
iw: City pause

t: San Jose rejects a moratorium and upholds a data center in an Nvidia building
b: The council voted 8–0 to deny a labor-led appeal. Draft standards for 20 MW-plus projects go to the council in December; Santa Clara also chose new rules over a pause.
iw: Silicon Valley stays open, with rules

t: Gilroy extends its moratorium, stalling a second Amazon data center
b: The September 45-day pause was extended while the city writes zoning, water, noise and energy standards. Amazon's first campus there is under construction.
iw: Blocks a large expansion

t: Palm Springs extends its data center moratorium to August 2028
b: The 22-month extension of an August urgency ordinance is the maximum state law allows.
iw: Two-year city pause

t: Indio adopts an urgency moratorium and moves toward a permanent ban
b: Adopted with no application pending. On Oct. 7 the council unanimously extended it a final time, to Oct. 16, 2027, while staff write permanent rules.
iw: Likely permanent ban

t: Brawley pauses large-scale data centers, 3–2
b: The council dropped a proposed one-year term while the city writes rules; its zoning code doesn't define data centers. Members Grass and Kelley voted no.
iw: City pause

t: Arcata, Angels Camp and Calaveras County adopt urgency data center moratoriums
b: Arcata voted unanimously Sept. 16. Angels Camp voted 5–0 on Aug. 18, and Calaveras County supervisors followed 4–0 on Aug. 25 for unincorporated areas.
iw: Spreading small pauses

t: Escondido and Lake Elsinore adopt 45-day data center pauses
b: Part of a wave of at least 26 California resolutions, moratoriums or bans since June, by one advocacy group's count.
iw: Short city pauses

t: California regulators tighten terms for Google's 250 MW PG&E hookup as Rule 30 stays open
b: A draft resolution approves the agreement but caps refunds and ties network upgrade costs to the pending Rule 30 decision on transmission-level service. PG&E and advocates reached a partial settlement in May.
iw: More upfront cost for big loads

t: BLM approves the first data center on federal public land, near Boulder City
b: It amended a 2023 solar right-of-way for Townsite Solar 2 instead of doing a new environmental review. The plan includes four buildings, a 70 MW battery and gas or biodiesel backup on desert tortoise habitat.
iw: Opens public land to data centers

t: Federal appeals board halts the Boulder City data center on public land
b: A judge found the city and environmental groups likely to prove BLM skipped required review. In October the board let BLM take the approval back for further review, which the city opposed while legal questions remain.
iw: Project stalled, precedent at risk

t: Titus bill would require full environmental review for data centers on public land
b: The Public Lands Accountability Act would bar shortcut approvals like the Boulder City right-of-way change. Neither industry nor environmental groups endorsed it.
iw: Slower federal-land path

t: Nevada approves 362 MW of private gas plants for Tract's Storey County data centers
b: The first gas plants approved specifically for Nevada data centers would run two to three years until NV Energy can serve the sites. They still need air and county permits; critics say they sidestep the renewable standard.
iw: Faster power for big campuses

t: Switch is behind a proposed 510 MW gas plant at the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center
b: Filed with regulators in June by Nexus Fulcrum LLC; Switch disclosed it is the intended owner and buyer of the power.
iw: Self-supplied power for growth

t: Alaska's data center ratepayer bill passes the Senate but dies in the House
b: SB 250 would have required commission-approved contracts making data centers bear their own costs, plus decommissioning plans. The Senate passed it 14–5; the sponsor plans to try again.
iw: No cost rules for now

t: Alaska backs leasing a square mile of North Slope land for a giant data center
b: A preliminary best-interest finding supports a 50-year lease for Stak Energy's $500 million campus, which could need 1 to 3 GW of power from North Slope gas. Federal wetlands permits are still needed.
iw: State land offered

t: Kreiss-Tomkins backs a data center moratorium; Bronson calls himself a big believer
b: The Democrat wants a pause until lawmakers pass a framework. Gov. Dunleavy, who is term-limited, has courted the industry.
iw: Candidates split

t: Hawaii County advances a bill to keep industrial-scale data centers off the island
b: Bill 170 would define data centers separately from small data processing sites and make them not permitted. A committee forwarded it 8–0; planning commissions are reviewing it, one with an unfavorable vote.
iw: Possible island-wide ban

t: Jackson County bans data centers in unincorporated areas
b: The unanimous ordinance replaced a one-year pause amid opposition to a proposed AI data center near Compass Lake. Commissioners also removed a provision that would have allowed exceptions.
iw: County ban

t: Franklin County, Georgia, adopts a data center moratorium
b: On the county attorney's advice, commissioners adopted a pause slightly shorter than the six months they had discussed. A commissioner had drafted an ordinance banning data centers outright.
iw: County pause

t: Tulsa pauses new data center approvals through the end of 2026
b: The unanimous pause runs about nine months, cut from a proposed year, with planning office updates every 60 days. Both phases of Project Anthem in east Tulsa, the first a Meta campus, are exempt.
iw: City pause with project exemptions

t: Beale withdraws Project Atlas in Coweta, Oklahoma
b: The developer pulled its rezoning for the 270-acre, four-phase campus after planners voted 4–1 in January to recommend denial and residents spent months pressing city leaders. It gave no reason.
iw: Project withdrawn

t: Oklahoma City pauses data center rezonings and permits through 2026
b: The unanimous emergency ordinance ends sooner if zoning rules pass and includes an appeal process. Two pending rezonings are exempt.
iw: City pause

t: Oklahoma City narrows its pause to data centers above 75 MW
b: The 7–2 amendment came after data center workers packed City Hall. It also exempts two named projects, which two councilors said raised questions of favoritism.
iw: Smaller projects can apply again

t: Oklahoma's proposed statewide data center moratorium dies without a vote
b: Sen. Kendal Sacchieri's SB 1488 would have paused data centers of 100 MW or more until Nov. 2029 while the Corporation Commission studied water, rates and siting. It never got a committee vote; she has since sought an interim study.
iw: Bill failed

t: El Paso requires council approval and 300-foot buffers for big data centers
b: The unanimous framework requires a special permit for hyperscale centers, 300 feet from homes, schools and parks, plus water and energy plans. In May the city stopped offering incentives. Meta's campus under construction is unaffected.
iw: Special permit and buffers

t: San Antonio votes Oct. 29 on data center zoning, not a pause
b: Only four council members backed a 90-to-180-day moratorium in August. The rules would limit data centers to industrial or heavy commercial zones, keep them 500 feet from homes and require council authorization.
iw: New siting limits

t: Brownsville's 90-day data center moratorium faces a final vote Nov. 4
b: Commissioners unanimously passed a first reading Oct. 7 after three hearings state law requires. The pause would cover the city and its extraterritorial jurisdiction and could be extended once while a task force studies data centers.
iw: Proposed city pause

t: Hawaii County planning commissions split on the Bill 170 data center ban
b: Windward planners voted 5–1 against it as too vague; Leeward planners unanimously backed it and suggested a moratorium. The bill returns to the County Council. No data center has applied.
iw: Island-wide ban advancing

t: Hawaii's energy office begins a working group on data centers
b: It follows legislative resolutions on data center costs and reports to lawmakers in 2027. The state energy officer says Hawaii lacks the bandwidth and cheap power developers want.
iw: Study only

t: Royalton voters ban AI and crypto data centers for five years
b: Approved on Town Meeting Day, making Royalton the first Vermont town to block data centers.
iw: Five-year town ban

t: Morristown, Vermont, adopts a two-year interim ban on data centers
b: The unanimous interim bylaw covers data centers and other high-impact uses while planners write permanent rules. No project has been proposed. It's the third Vermont town to act since the governor's veto of statewide rules.
iw: Two-year town pause

t: About two-thirds of Vermonters back a statewide ban on large data centers
b: The Vermont Public poll comes after Gov. Phil Scott vetoed a bill to regulate large data centers, saying existing rules are enough.
iw: Poll

t: Anchorage adds data centers to its zoning code, 10–2
b: No large data center has been proposed. Projects now face public review and must show utilities can supply the power.
iw: New review step

t: Mat-Su Assembly overrides a veto to court a data center developer
b: The 6–1 vote sets a two-year partnership with Terra Energy Center to find a large power user for borough land near Port MacKenzie or Big Lake, an anchor customer for a proposed coal plant.
iw: Borough courting projects

t: Senators question a 20,000-acre land transfer for possible Mat-Su data centers
b: Five committee members said the state's plan to give the land to AIDEA is too vague to judge, and a legislative attorney flagged legal issues. Chair Cathy Giessel backs a moratorium until lawmakers set rules.
iw: Could stall a state-backed site

t: Davidson County deadlocks 3–3 on a data center pause
b: The six-month moratorium failed on a tie after a public hearing. The county currently treats data centers as warehouses and has had inquiries but no formal applications.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Davidson County holds a hearing on a four-month data center pause
b: Commissioners voted 4–2 on Sept. 28 to bring back a shorter moratorium. The chair opposed it, saying projects would move to neighboring counties.
iw: Proposed county pause
